homework.q: Take the paper “A Temperature Ceiling for Evaporating Primordial Black Holes from the Density Bound”. Its stated result is: This paper reports a computation from stated assumptions (status: simulated, not measured) on a Temperature Ceiling for Evaporating Primordial Black Holes from the Density Bound. Headline computed values: M min g = 1.000e+13; T max K = 1.227e+13; T max MeV = 1.057e+03; T Pl K = 1.417e+32. (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong.
homework.worked: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

classes.title: The Bounce & the Aldred Limit

papers.t: Binary-Pulsar Orbital Decay as a Test of the Bounce Frame
papers.r: Binary-pulsar decay bounds any extra orbital energy loss below about half a percent, while the bounce frame predicts a modification of order ten to the minus forty — so the channel is settled-neutral for the frame, stated with the thirty-seven-order margin attached, and remains a front-line test only for frameworks whose deviations turn on at stellar compactness.

papers.t: Particle Production in an Expanding Condensate as a Quantitative Analogue of a Cosmological Bounce
papers.r: Computed headline values for this analogue system are: eps_mid = 0.45, n_mid = 0.168, n_deep = 0.548, ratio = 1.48e-63, rho_lab = 1.44e-05. The study is simulated and computed from stated assumptions and published experimental scales, not measured, and every value is reproducible from the deposited calculation script and results file.

papers.t: Pulsar Timing Residuals as a Bound on Bounce Shear
papers.r: Pulsar timing bounds any steady local shear rate below roughly ten to the minus twenty-third per second, forty-seven orders of magnitude below the bounce ceiling rate, with the gap bridged by the expansion dilution the framework predicts.

papers.t: The Dispersion Measure–Distance Relation in a Bounced Cosmology
papers.r: The dispersion measure–distance relation in a bounced cosmology is numerically identical to the standard relation at every redshift where bursts are observed, with a fractional difference at redshift 1 that is effectively zero beside a host-modelling uncertainty of order twenty percent.

papers.t: The Pulsar Timing Array Background and the Bounce Prediction
papers.r: The nanohertz background measured by the timing arrays corresponds to an energy fraction near ten to the minus eighth; reproducing it from the bounce would require a turnaround shear fraction of a few percent, and a ceiling-level sheared turnaround would overproduce it by a factor of several tens. Pulsar timing therefore genuinely constrains the bounce's anisotropy — the strongest frame test in this territory.

papers.t: A Joint Bound on the Bounce Amplitude from the Full Distance Ladder: Fisher Combination of Sixteen Rungs
papers.r: This paper combines the rung-by-rung frame sensitivities computed across the distance ladder into a single bound on the bounce amplitude, using a Fisher combination of the independent tolerances. Treating each probe's tolerance as a Gaussian constraint on the asymptotic amplitude epsilon, the acoustic transverse and radial modes, the sound horizon, the supernova diagram, the chronometers, and the time-delay distances

papers.t: Calibrating the Sound Horizon in a Bounced Cosmology: The Drag-Epoch Integral and Its Error Budget
papers.r: The sound horizon at the drag epoch is the length that turns angular and redshift separations into distances, and its value is an integral over the expansion rate in the first few hundred thousand years. Evaluating that integral in a bounced cosmology, with the correction fully switched on at the relevant redshifts, shortens the horizon from 141.56 Mpc to 134.97 Mpc at epsilon = 0.10, a change of -4.65 percent.

papers.t: Carbon-Star J-Branch Distances in a Bounced Cosmology: A Young Method Audited for Frame Sensitivity
papers.r: The J-region asymptotic giant branch method uses carbon stars whose J-band luminosities cluster tightly, and it has quickly become a cross-check on both Cepheid and red-giant distances to supernova hosts.

papers.t: Cosmic Chronometers in a Bounced Cosmology: Differential Ages and the Expansion Rate They Return
papers.r: Cosmic chronometers read the expansion rate directly from the age difference of passively evolving galaxies, and in a bounced cosmology that reading changes exactly where the bounce correction switches on.

papers.t: Gravitational-Wave Standard Siren Distances in a Bounced Cosmology: From GW170817 to Third-Generation Reach
papers.r: Gravitational-wave standard sirens measure luminosity distance from the waveform alone, and their sensitivity to a bounced cosmology grows steeply with the redshift their detectors reach. The nearby event GW170817, at about 44 Mpc, has its distance interpretation shifted by -0.009 percent at epsilon = 0.10, far below its 15 percent distance uncertainty.

papers.t: Megamaser Geometric Distances in a Bounced Cosmology: The Maser Cosmology Project Sample Recomputed
papers.r: Water megamasers in accretion discs give geometric distances to galaxies well beyond the Local Group, and recomputing the Maser Cosmology Project sample in a bounced cosmology tests whether those distances, and the Hubble constant drawn from them, depend on the frame.

papers.t: Mira Variable Distances in a Bounced Cosmology: Period-Luminosity Relations Beyond the Local Group
papers.r: Mira variables, the long-period pulsators of old and intermediate-age populations, extend standard-candle distances to galaxies without young stars, and their period-luminosity relation has been used to measure the expansion rate from the maser galaxy NGC 4258 outward.

papers.t: RR Lyrae Distances in a Bounced Cosmology: Globular Cluster Scales and the Population II Ladder
papers.r: RR Lyrae stars carry a second, older distance ladder through globular clusters and galactic haloes, and recomputing that ladder in a bounced cosmology shows it to be as frame-insensitive as the Cepheid ladder it parallels.

papers.t: Strong-Lens Time-Delay Distances in a Bounced Cosmology: The Distance Combination and Its Sensitivity
papers.r: Strong gravitational lens time delays measure a combination of angular diameter distances to the lens, to the source, and between them, and that combination samples intermediate redshifts where a bounce correction is partly switched on.

papers.t: Surface Brightness Fluctuation Distances in a Bounced Cosmology: Elliptical Galaxy Moduli and Their Frame Margin
papers.r: Surface brightness fluctuations measure distances to elliptical galaxies from the graininess of their unresolved starlight, reaching well into the Hubble flow with per-galaxy precision near five percent.

papers.t: The Alcock-Paczynski Test with Stacked Voids: Sensitivity to the Expansion History and to a Bounce Rescaling
papers.r: At redshift 0.5 the Alcock-Paczynski product takes the value 0.580. Analysing that stack with matter fraction 0.25 gives an apparent axis ratio of 1.024 instead of unity. At redshift 1.0 the product rises to 1.369. The corresponding wrong-cosmology axis ratio at redshift 1.0 is 1.037.

papers.t: The Cepheid Period-Luminosity Zero Point in a Bounced Cosmology: Anchor Distances and the Size of the Correction
papers.r: Recomputing the three geometric anchors of the Cepheid distance scale in a bounced cosmology changes almost nothing locally, and that null result is itself informative. For the asymptotic bounce amplitude favoured by early-universe considerations, epsilon = 0.10, the distance modulus of the Large Magellanic Cloud anchor shifts by 2.36e-07 mag, the maser galaxy NGC 4258 by 0.00004 mag, and a Milky Way Cepheid at 2 kpc

papers.t: The Gaia Parallax Anchor in a Bounced Cosmology: Whether the Zero Point of the Ladder Can Move
papers.r: Every distance in the ladder ultimately rests on trigonometric parallax, and this paper asks whether that foundation is frame-dependent. It is not, and the computation makes the non-dependence quantitative.

papers.t: The Integrated Sachs-Wolfe Signal of Stacked Supervoids: An Amplitude Test Against the Bounce Expansion History
papers.r: For the Granett-type supervoid the standard calculation predicts a stacked temperature shift of -6.5 microkelvin. Applying the bounce decay factor moves that prediction only to -6.3 microkelvin. A typical catalogue void of 45 megaparsecs per h contributes just -0.8 microkelvin, far below single-patch noise. The Eridanus-scale structure, by virtue of its size, reaches -14.5 microkelvin in the same calculation.

papers.t: The Radial Baryon Acoustic Oscillation Scale in a Bounced Cosmology: Direct Expansion Rates Against Survey Values
papers.r: The radial baryon acoustic oscillation measurement returns the product of the expansion rate and the sound horizon at the tracer redshift, a direct reading of H(z) against a computed length. In the bounce frame both factors move, the horizon shrinking and the rate rising, and their product at epsilon = 0.10 changes by -3.57 percent at redshift 0.5, -2.45 percent at redshift 1.0, and -1.62 percent at redshift 1.5.

papers.t: The Transverse Baryon Acoustic Oscillation Scale in a Bounced Cosmology: Angular Diameter Distances Against Survey Values
papers.r: The transverse baryon acoustic oscillation measurement compares an angular scale on the sky with the comoving distance to the tracer redshift, and in a bounced cosmology that distance carries an integrated memory of the early correction.

papers.t: The Void Size Function in a Bounced Cosmology: A Shear-Bound Correction and a Count Test
papers.r: At redshift zero the standard calculation places 1.85e+04 voids per cubic gigaparsec per h in the bin centred near 30 megaparsecs per h. By redshift one the same bin has emptied to 7.56e+03 per cubic gigaparsec per h, reflecting the shorter time available for large underdensities to evacuate. At 50 megaparsecs per h the bounced calculation predicts a fraction 0.960 of the standard abundance.

papers.t: Tip of the Red Giant Branch Calibration in a Bounced Cosmology: Halo Distances and the Zero Point Shift
papers.r: The tip of the red giant branch offers a distance indicator whose calibration is stellar physics rather than expansion history, and recomputing its ladder in a bounced cosmology quantifies that independence.

papers.t: Tully-Fisher Distances in a Bounced Cosmology: Rotation-Based Moduli and the Peculiar Velocity Field
papers.r: The Tully-Fisher relation turns a spiral galaxy's rotation speed into a luminosity and hence a distance, and it is the workhorse of peculiar-velocity cosmology. Recomputing Tully-Fisher distances in a bounced cosmology separates two effects that are often conflated.

papers.t: Type Ia Supernova Distance Moduli in a Bounced Cosmology: Residuals Across Redshift and the Amplitude They Permit
papers.r: Type Ia supernovae are the first distance-ladder rung that genuinely samples the redshifts where a bounce correction switches on, and their moduli bound the correction directly. Relative to the standard frame, the bounce frame at asymptotic amplitude epsilon = 0.10 changes distance moduli by -0.0021 mag at redshift 0.1, -0.0112 mag at redshift 0.5, -0.0221 mag at redshift 1.0, and -0.0376 mag at redshift 2.0.

papers.t: Void Density Profiles and the Shear Ceiling: How Empty a Bounced Cosmology Allows a Void to Become
papers.r: At the centre the fitted profile sits at 0.150 of the cosmic mean density. At half the void radius the density has recovered only to 0.417 of the mean, so the inner half of a void is close to uniformly deep. At the void radius itself the profile reaches 1.100 of the mean, the compensation ridge formed by evacuated material.

papers.t: Characteristic Strain of the Nanohertz Background in the Bounce Frame
papers.r: This paper asks a single question: How large is the nanohertz characteristic strain if the published common-process amplitude is read through a bounce cosmology, and where does the bounce contribution sit relative to the astrophysical signal? Working from the published common-process amplitude of 2.4e-15 in characteristic strain at one cycle per year and the standard binary spectral index of thirteen thirds, the stud

papers.t: Lensing Potential Power in a Bounced Cosmology: Scale-Dependent Suppression Below the Bounce Multipole
papers.r: The bounce imprint suppresses lensing power by 0.169 at multipole 10 and 0.00000 at multipole 1000; the integrated lensing power ratio is 0.837, the low-multipole B-mode power ratio is 0.837 (equivalent tensor-to-scalar level 0.0084), delensing residuals move from 0.250 to 0.372, and the total reconstruction signal-to-noise for the stated configuration is 15.3. Computed from stated assumptions, not measured.

papers.t: Acoustic-Peak Smoothing as a Bounce Bound: Lensing Smearing of the Temperature Spectrum
papers.r: The bounce imprint suppresses lensing power by 0.176 at multipole 10 and 0.00000 at multipole 1000; the integrated lensing power ratio is 0.831, the low-multipole B-mode power ratio is 0.831 (equivalent tensor-to-scalar level 0.0083), delensing residuals move from 0.250 to 0.377, and the total reconstruction signal-to-noise for the stated configuration is 15.2. classes.lesson: Mind the threshold; you are stepping into deep time. I am Professor Aurelia Voss, and this is The Bounce & the Aldred Limit — a class in Cosmology at Exolex University. The syllabus is real: 106 papers from the Aldred corpus, every one deposited and citable, and in this room we read them for what they actually claim. First, Binary-Pulsar Orbital Decay as a Test of the Bounce Frame. Its stated result: Binary-pulsar decay bounds any extra orbital energy loss below about half a percent, while the bounce frame predicts a modification of order ten to the minus forty — so the channel is settled-neutral for the frame, stated with the thirty-seven-order margin att Next, Particle Production in an Expanding Condensate as a Quantitative Analogue of a Cosmological Bounce. Its stated result: Computed headline values for this analogue system are — the figures themselves are in the deposit, and on your syllabus. And then, Pulsar Timing Residuals as a Bound on Bounce Shear. Its stated result: Pulsar timing bounds any steady local shear rate below roughly ten to the minus twenty-third per second, forty-seven orders of magnitude below the bounce ceiling rate, with the gap bridged by the expansion dilution the framework predicts. That is the shape of this class: real claims, real numbers, and the arguments between them. Your homework is waiting on your desk.

papers.t: Big Bang Nucleosynthesis in the Aldred Frame: An Expansion-Rate Bound from the Light Elements
papers.r: At BBN densities the Aldred frame shifts the expansion rate by at most 4.22e-50 and Y_p by 1.67e-51 — 48 orders below observational error — and its effects would register only near 4.66e53 g/cm^3, within an order of magnitude of the limit itself.

papers.t: Black-Hole Bookkeeping in the Aldred Frame: The Bounced Core, the Remnant Floor, and What Evaporation Leaves Behind
papers.r: Evaporation in the Aldred frame stops at a remnant floor of 8.66e13 g (up to 6.37e14 g for concentrated cores) whose Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of 1.99e38 k_B is only 3.85 times its baryon-count entropy, while the fully accumulated bounced core of a solar-mass collapse is 3.66e-8 cm in radius.

papers.t: Can Dynamics Close the Laboratory Gap? Rotating and Oscillating Spin-Polarised Sources in the Aldred Frame
papers.r: Dynamics buys at most 16.4 orders of magnitude (13.7 without a deliberate double count) against static laboratory gaps of 24.9-49 orders for the Aldred Limit, so no rotation, resonance, integration schedule, or cryogenic spin ensemble closes the gap.

papers.t: Energy Bookkeeping of a Transit in the Aldred Frame: What a Passage Costs and Where the Energy Goes
papers.r: A one-metre transit throat at 99% of the Aldred Limit costs 3.62×10⁷⁵ J to assemble (8.65×10⁷¹ J per kilogram of payload), the energy is returned in full on closure by the bounce, and the holding power and the returned-energy partition are open terms the frame cannot close.

papers.t: Fifth-Coordinate Consequences for Laboratory Clocks: Drift Bounds from Optical Clock Comparisons
papers.r: Optical-clock null comparisons bound the fifth-coordinate clock coupling to |kappa_5| < 10^-18 m^-1 at a 1 m separation (product bound |kappa_5 Delta chi| < 10^-18), 52.8 orders below the inverse Planck length.

papers.t: Gravitational-Wave Propagation in the Aldred Frame: Speed, Luminosity Distance, and the Bounds from GW170817
papers.r: Gravitational waves get exactly no speed or distance correction in vacuum in this frame, and at most 2.05×10⁻⁴⁰ anywhere on a realistic path — far below anything GW170817 could have seen.

papers.t: Ordinary Stars in the Aldred Frame: Main-Sequence Structure, Lifetimes, and the Densest Stellar Interiors
papers.r: The spin-torsion correction is negligible in every stable star — largest 1.03×10⁻⁴⁵ in an iron core at collapse onset — and becomes large only in the final approach to the bounce density.

papers.t: Solar-System Bounds on the Aldred Frame: Perihelion Precession, Frame Dragging, and Light Travel Time
papers.r: Torsion vanishes in vacuum in this frame, so Mercury's perihelion, frame dragging, and the Shapiro delay all receive exactly the general-relativistic prediction, and the frame's largest interior correction anywhere in the solar system is 1.54×10⁻⁵³ at the solar core.

papers.t: Structure Formation After a Finite-Density Bounce: The Growth Factor and σ₈ in the Aldred Frame
papers.r: Integrating the linear growth equation from the finite-density bounce to today shifts σ₈ by only −2.7×10⁻⁸ relative to ΛCDM, so the Aldred frame moves S₈ toward the low-redshift values by nothing measurable and leaves the S₈ tension unchanged.

papers.t: THE COUNT IMPOSSIBILITY — Constructions 1–14 Assembled
papers.r: Constructions 1-14 assembled: the count cannot be produced from the frame contents as stated; the road is closed.

papers.t: The Aldred Limit in the Laboratory: The Einstein-Cartan Spin-Torsion Correction at Terrestrial Densities
papers.r: rho_A recomputed at 9.720e54 g/cm3 from constants; the largest terrestrial density ratio (osmium) is 2.32e-54 - shortfalls of 49/44/35.5 orders by channel.

papers.r: Derives the maximum spin-density bound (rho_A = 9.720e54 g/cm3); past it, collapse bounces instead of reaching a singularity.

papers.r: The CMB axis claim now has a registered, falsifiable azimuthal-average prediction (extrema at 0° / 68.69° / 123.40° / 180°, depth ratios 1 : 0.386 : 0.264 : 0.363, axis depth capped at 68.1 µK), and the Cold Spot's depth cannot be the predicted ring's depth under the stated no-cancellation assumption.

papers.r: The Einstein–Cartan torsion correction shifts the Chandrasekhar mass by only 7.29×10⁻⁴⁶ in fraction at a massive white dwarf's central density, so the Type Ia standard-candle mass is unmoved at any observable level.

papers.r: A collapse floor for fermionic matter - the floor that later meets the evaporation remnant floor at 8.66e13 g.

papers.t: The Collapse Floor: The Smallest Black Hole the Aldred Frame Allows to Form
papers.r: The smallest black hole that can form by collapse in the Aldred frame is 8.66×10^13 g for a uniform sphere (1.29×10^14 g for a concentrated parabolic profile), and the uniform collapse floor coincides with the evaporation remnant floor of 8.66×10^13 g to within 0.02 percent.

papers.t: The Fifth Coordinate — the Worldsheet-Flux Law for Θ
papers.r: Theta gets a worldsheet-flux law and an allowed band [4.40e-3, 7.54e-3] rad; the value itself is not derived.

papers.t: The Flatness Problem Through the Aldred Bounce: Bookkeeping of the Curvature Fraction Across Contraction and Expansion
papers.r: A radiation contraction to the Aldred bounce removes 36.6 of the 42.6 orders of flatness tuning (a stiff contraction removes 48.9), but the contraction's duration and content are not supplied by the frame, so the bounce alone does not finish the job.

papers.t: The Horizon Problem in a Bouncing Universe: Causal Bookkeeping Through the Aldred Bounce
papers.r: Full-sky causal contact through the Aldred bounce requires the equivalent of 46.8 inflationary e-folds of horizon — a condition the Einstein–Cartan frame permits but does not itself supply, since it fixes neither the contracting branch's equation of state nor its duration.

papers.t: The Inspiral Phase in the Aldred Frame: Torsion Corrections to Binary Waveforms and the LIGO–Virgo Bound
papers.r: The torsion correction dephases a LIGO-band neutron-star inspiral by 8.60×10⁻³⁷ cycles at the densest realistic centre — 35.1 orders of magnitude below the 0.1-cycle phase accuracy of GW170817-class measurements — and near-limit binaries merge at 5.05×10²² Hz with inspiral times 17.1 orders beyond the Hubble time, so no conceivable detector sees the effect.

papers.t: The Primordial Power Spectrum Across a Finite-Density Bounce: Bounds on the Spectral Index and Its Running
papers.r: Planck's measured spectral index bounds the density at which the observable spectrum is laid down across an Einstein–Cartan bounce to ρ_b ≤ 2.77×10⁵⁴ g/cm³ (1σ), and no spectrum is produced at or above half the Aldred Limit under the stated matching prescription.

papers.t: The Surviving Count in a Torsion-Regulated Vacuum: An Equilibrium-Thickness Construction, Its Executed Censuses, and the Kinetic Law It Lacks
papers.r: Builds an equilibrium-thickness construction for the surviving count, executes its censuses, and names the kinetic law it still lacks.

papers.t: The Vacuum Density in the Bounce Frame: Dissolution of the 10¹²² Gap, the Count That Survives It, and a Landing at a Factor of 6.0
papers.r: The naive mode count is a bookkeeping error (dissolution); the paper presents a surviving count landing at a factor of 6.0 - later house work (24082360) found the count cannot be completed as stated.

papers.t: Torsion Corrections to Compact-Star Structure: Mass–Radius Shifts and the Maximum Mass in the Aldred Frame
papers.r: The Aldred-frame torsion correction shifts the SLy maximum mass by only −8.9×10⁻⁴¹ in fractional terms, leaving compact-star structure unchanged at any measurable level, with the correction reaching 10⁻⁶ only at 9.72×10⁴⁸ g/cm³.

papers.t: Two Bounds and an Integration Constant: The Kopczyński–Trautman pin, the de Sitter floor, and the open value problem
papers.r: The Kopczynski-Trautman pin and the de Sitter floor bound the frame; the integration constant value stays open.

homework.q: Take the paper “Big Bang Nucleosynthesis in the Aldred Frame: An Expansion-Rate Bound from the Light Elements”. Its stated result is: At BBN densities the Aldred frame shifts the expansion rate by at most 4.22e-50 and Y_p by 1.67e-51 — 48 orders below observational error — and its effects would register only near 4.66e53 g/cm^3, within an order of magnitude of the limit itself. (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong.

classes.title: The Aldred Limit and Its Consequence Tree

papers.t: Carrier Branches of the Aldred Limit: Which Fermion Sets the Bound in a Given Matter
papers.r: The Aldred Limit density scales as the square of the mass of the fermion whose spin sources the torsion. That single scaling produces a family of bounds, one per carrier, spanning an enormous range: from 1.10e+35 g per cubic centimetre for a 0.1 eV neutrino to 9.72e+54 g per cubic centimetre for the neutron, a span of 3.16e+20 in density.

papers.t: Coherent Versus Incoherent Spin: The Rescaling of the Aldred Limit When Spins Align
papers.r: The standard Aldred Limit assumes randomly oriented spins. If spins align coherently inside domains, the spin density that sources torsion is enhanced, and the bound density falls in inverse proportion to the number of coherently aligned spins per domain.

papers.t: The Energy Budget of a Bounced Core: Gravitational Release at the Aldred Limit Against the Supernova Scale
papers.r: What energy does a bounce at the Aldred Limit have to dispose of? Bringing a uniform 1.4 solar mass core from a large radius to its bounce radius of 0.0 m releases a gravitational self-energy of 7.589e+59 J. That is 7.589e+15 times the canonical kinetic energy of a core-collapse supernova (1e44 J) and 25296825610841.1 times the entire neutrino energy budget of such an event (3e46 J).

papers.t: The Entropy of a Bounced Core: Thermal Entropy at the Aldred Limit Against the Area Bound
papers.r: Assigning the bounced core's energy density entirely to heat, the most entropy the core can hold, a 1.4 solar mass core at the Aldred Limit carries a thermal entropy of 7.371e+47 in units of Boltzmann's constant, or 0.0 per baryon. The Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of a black hole of the same mass is 2.056e+77, larger by a factor that makes the core's thermal entropy a fraction 3.585e-30 of the area bound.

papers.t: The Fastest Rotation at the Limit: A Period Floor for a Bounced Core
papers.r: A bounced core at the Aldred Limit cannot rotate faster than its mass-shedding limit, and because its density is fixed by the bound, that limit is a pure number of the framework: Omega_max = square root of (4 pi G rho_A/3), independent of the core's mass. On the neutron branch the corresponding period floor is 3.812e-24 s, a rotation frequency of 2.623e+23 Hz. On the electron branch the floor is 7.009e-21 s.

papers.t: The Minimum Radius of a Bounced Core: Where the Aldred Limit Sits Against the Schwarzschild Radius
papers.r: A mass that collapses to the Aldred Limit cannot be compressed further, so it has a minimum radius R_min = (3M/(4 pi rho_A))^(1/3). This paper computes that radius for masses from 0.1 to a million solar masses and compares it with the Schwarzschild radius of the same mass.

papers.t: The Rotation-Displaced Bounce: How Far Below the Aldred Limit a Spinning Core Turns Around
papers.r: The Aldred Limit density rho_A = 9.72e+54 g per cubic centimetre is the turnaround density of a non-rotating collapse. Real cores rotate, and rotation supplies part of the support against gravity, so a spinning core should turn around below the Limit.

papers.t: The Shear Threshold at the Aldred Limit: How Much Anisotropy a Spin-Torsion Bounce Can Survive
papers.r: In a homogeneous but anisotropic collapse of Bianchi I type, shear acts as an additional positive energy density and competes with the negative spin-torsion term that produces the Aldred Limit bounce. This paper computes the largest shear the bounce can survive.

papers.t: The Smallest Size of a Bouncing Universe: Scale Factor, Horizon, and Density at the Aldred Limit
papers.r: If the observable universe bounced at the Aldred Limit instead of beginning at a singularity, it had a smallest size, and this paper computes it. Compressing the stated mass-energy of the observable universe, 1.5e53 kg, uniformly to the neutron-branch Limit density gives a minimum radius of 0.0 m.

papers.t: The Smallest Structure at the Limit: A Jeans Length for the Bounce Era
papers.r: At the Aldred Limit, pressure and gravity balance on a definite scale, the Jeans length, and no smaller self-gravitating structure can form or survive the bounce era. With the relativistic sound speed c over root 3 at the bound density, the Jeans length is 0.00 m and the corresponding Jeans mass is 2.813e+11 kg. The minimum-size patch of the observable universe, 0.0 m in radius, contains 5.333e+41 such Jeans volumes.

papers.t: The Spin Density at the Bound: Counting Aligned Angular Momentum at the Aldred Limit
papers.r: The Aldred Limit is a statement about spin density, and this paper counts the spins. At the bound density the neutron number density is 5.802e+84 per cubic metre, giving an incoherent spin density of 3.059e+50 in SI units. A 1.4 solar mass bounced core contains 1.662e+57 neutrons.

papers.t: The Temperature at the Bounce: A Radiation-Equivalent Ceiling from the Aldred Limit
papers.r: A density bound implies a temperature ceiling wherever the matter is hot enough for its energy to be counted thermally. Converting the Aldred Limit density into a radiation-equivalent temperature through u = a T^4 gives, for the neutron branch, a ceiling of 3.278e+22 K.

papers.t: The Bound for a Mixture: Composition Weighting of the Aldred Limit in Multi-Carrier Matter
papers.r: Real matter is a mixture, and a density bound derived carrier by carrier needs a composition rule. This paper derives one from the additivity of the spin-torsion source: with mass fractions w_i, the effective bound satisfies 1/rho_A,mix = sum of w_i squared over rho_A,i. Applied to neutron matter with ten percent protons by mass, the bound moves from 9.72e+54 to 1.19e+55 g per cubic centimetre, a factor 1.219.

papers.t: The Aldred Limit Inside a Neutron Star: A Computed Absence and What It Excludes
papers.r: If the Aldred Limit is correct, its effects inside a neutron star are computable, and this paper computes them: at five times nuclear saturation density, near the top of the plausible range for neutron star centres, the Einstein-Cartan spin-torsion correction to the effective density is a fraction 1.44e-40 of the density itself.

papers.t: Timescales of the Bounce: Free-Fall, Sound-Crossing, and Torsion Response at the Aldred Limit
papers.r: Three timescales govern a bounce at the Aldred Limit: the free-fall time of matter at the bound density, the sound-crossing time of the bounced core, and the response time of the torsion field implied by the Cartan equation. This paper computes all three.

papers.t: The Torsion Bound in Inverse Metres: A Length Scale for the Aldred Limit and Its Reach
papers.r: The Aldred Limit can be stated as a bound on torsion itself: through the Cartan equation, T_A = square root of (8 pi G rho_A / c squared). On the neutron branch T_A is 1.347e+16 per metre, a characteristic length of 7.425e-17 m. That length is 4.594e+18 times the Planck length and a factor 2.8 below the neutron Compton wavelength.

papers.t: Why the Neutrino Branch Does Not Bind: A Disproof of the Lightest-Carrier Objection
papers.r: A common objection to the neutron-branch Aldred Limit runs as follows: neutrinos are far lighter than neutrons, their branch of the bound lies far lower, and the lightest carrier present should set the operative bound, so collapse should bounce at the neutrino branch density of 1.10e+35 g per cubic centimetre. This paper shows the objection fails on its own terms.

classes.title: Vacuum Dissolution and the Surviving Count

papers.t: Thirty Micrometres: The Plate Separation at Which the Casimir Energy Density Equals the Cosmic Vacuum Density
papers.r: Inverting the parallel-plate Casimir formula, the plate separation at which the magnitude of the Casimir energy density equals the observed cosmic vacuum density of 5.25 x 10^-10 J/m^3 is 30.1 micrometres, verified by substitution; across separations from ten nanometres to one millimetre the density crosses the cosmic value at that row, and the crossing moves by less than twenty percent if the cosmic density changes

papers.t: The Condensate Account: Vacuum Energy Stored in the Gluon and Quark Condensates and the Bag Constant
papers.r: Four standard phenomenological measures of QCD vacuum structure, the gluon condensate (0.012 GeV^4), the quark condensate scale (0.24 GeV), the MIT bag constant (fourth root 0.145 GeV), and a chiral scale of 0.30 GeV, correspond to energy densities exceeding the observed vacuum density by between 43.2 and 44.7 orders of magnitude; arising only after the QCD transition, they cannot be pre-empted by any early-universe

papers.t: The Cutoff Ladder: Zero-Point Energy Density at Eight Scales and the Fraction That Would Have to Survive at Each
papers.r: Evaluating the zero-point integral Lambda^4/(16 pi^2) at eight cutoffs against an observed vacuum density of 2.52 x 10^-47 GeV^4 (derived from H0 = 67.4 km/s/Mpc, Omega_Lambda = 0.685), the Planck-scale value exceeds the observed density by 120.7 orders of magnitude, the electroweak value by 54.0 orders, and even the QCD-scale value by 41.6 orders; only a cutoff near the neutrino mass scale approaches the target, and

papers.t: One Lifetime Cannot Do It: Exponential Dissolution of a Large Vacuum Density Fails Nucleosynthesis and Today Simultaneously
papers.r: Single-exponential dissolution of a once-large vacuum density is excluded: matching today's density from the Planck zero-point estimate requires a lifetime of 0.05 billion years while nucleosynthesis permits at most 5.06 x 10^-3 seconds, a conflict by a factor of 3.09 x 10^17, with the same conflict at factors of 1.52 x 10^17 (electroweak) and 6.76 x 10^16 (QCD initial densities).

papers.t: Excluded by History: The Vacuum Density Each Cosmic Epoch Tolerates, From Nucleosynthesis to Recombination
papers.r: Each radiation-dominated epoch caps the vacuum density at its own radiation density: nucleosynthesis (T = 1 MeV) tolerates at most 1.40 x 10^35 times the observed density, while an electroweak-scale vacuum density would have dominated the expansion below 28.5 GeV and a QCD-scale estimate below 0.027 GeV, both far above the nucleosynthesis temperature and therefore excluded by the verified history of the early univers

papers.t: Expansion Does Not Dilute a Vacuum: The Equation of State the Dilution Story Would Require
papers.r: The popular claim that cosmic expansion diluted a once-large vacuum energy to the observed value fails arithmetically: granting a Planck-cutoff initial density and the full expansion since the Planck era (a factor of 5.19 x 10^31), a true vacuum with w = -1 is diluted by a factor of exactly one, and reaching the observed density would require w = +0.27, close to the equation of state of radiation.

papers.t: Still Here After 13.8 Billion Years: The Decay-Rate Bound Implied by the Survival of the Present Vacuum
papers.r: Approximating our past spacetime volume by the Hubble volume times the Hubble time, the survival of the present vacuum bounds its decay rate density below 1.02 x 10^-168 GeV^4, implying minimum bounce actions of 563 (Planck-scale prefactor), 537 (grand-unification), 405 (electroweak), and 380 (QCD); relaxing the survival probability to one percent weakens the bound by less than a factor of five.

papers.t: What a Litre of Vacuum Would Weigh: Mass Equivalents of Zero-Point Densities From a Bottle to the Observable Universe
papers.r: Converted to mass equivalents, a litre of vacuum carries about 6 x 10^-30 kg at the observed density, about 5 x 10^24 kg at the electroweak-cutoff estimate, and about 3 x 10^91 kg at the Planck-cutoff estimate; the Planck-cutoff vacuum in the observable universe's volume would outweigh its entire critical-density mass-energy budget by a factor of about 10^121.

papers.t: The Depth of the Higgs Potential: A Measured Contribution Fifty-Five Orders Larger Than the Vacuum Density Observed
papers.r: From the measured Higgs mass of 125.25 GeV and vacuum expectation value of 246.22 GeV, the Higgs potential at its minimum contributes -1.19 x 10^8 GeV^4, computed in two algebraically equivalent forms that agree to machine precision; its magnitude exceeds the observed vacuum density by a factor of 4.72 x 10^54, so all other contributions must cancel it to 54.7 decimal digits and leave a small positive residue.

papers.t: The Holographic Coefficient: What Three Infrared Cutoffs Require of c_h^2 to Match the Observed Vacuum Density
papers.r: The holographic formula rho = 3 c_h^2 M_pl^2/L^2 with a unit coefficient gives 1.46, 1.03, and 0.14 times the observed vacuum density for the Hubble radius, future event horizon, and particle horizon respectively; matching observation requires c_h^2 of 0.685, 0.970, and 7.01, so the infrared idea supplies the order of magnitude while the coefficient remains an input fitted to the answer.

papers.t: The Coldest Thermometer in Physics: Temperature, Entropy, and Energy of the Present Vacuum's Horizon
papers.r: The present vacuum's horizon has a radius of 1.37 x 10^26 m, a Gibbons-Hawking temperature of 2.66 x 10^-30 K, and an entropy of 2.27 x 10^122 Boltzmann units; the enclosed vacuum energy of 5.69 x 10^69 J divided by the entropy agrees with k_B T to within a factor of 0.68, verifying the horizon identity in the arithmetic.

papers.t: Neutrino Masses and the Vacuum Scale: A Fourth-Power Sum That Overshoots by Five Orders of Magnitude
papers.r: Using the neutrino masses fixed by oscillation experiments (mass-squared differences 7.4 x 10^-5 and 2.5 x 10^-3 eV^2, normal ordering), the sum of fourth powers of the three masses is 6.26 x 10^-6 eV^4 even when the lightest mass vanishes, exceeding the observed vacuum density of 2.52 x 10^-11 eV^4 by a factor of about 248,000; a standard loop factor reduces the overshoot to about 1,570 but does not close it.

papers.t: The Lightest Field in Physics: Mass and Excursion Required of a Scalar That Rolls at the Observed Vacuum Density
papers.r: A scalar field whose quadratic potential equals the observed vacuum density today must have a mass within about an order of magnitude of hbar H0 (1.44 x 10^-33 eV): at exactly that mass it sits at 2.03 reduced Planck masses with a slow-roll parameter of 0.49, masses twice as large already exceed the slow-roll bound, and flatter potentials are bought only with field excursions beyond fourteen Planck masses.

papers.t: Radiative Instability: How Far the Vacuum Density Runs Between the Electroweak and Planck Scales
papers.r: A stated one-loop estimate for five Standard Model species (Higgs, W, Z, top, tau) shows the fitted vacuum density shifting by -1.21 x 10^9 GeV^4 between 246 GeV and the Planck scale, about 4.79 x 10^55 times the observed density itself, with the top quark dominating and boson-fermion cancellation reducing the total by less than an order of magnitude; the observed smallness is radiatively unstable in a precisely quan

papers.t: Broken Supersymmetry Leaves Too Much: The Breaking Scale That the Observed Vacuum Density Would Require
papers.r: With the residual density from broken supersymmetry taken as M_S^4/(16 pi^2), matching the observed density requires a breaking scale of 7.94 x 10^-12 GeV, a few milli-electronvolts; breaking at 1 TeV, the region indicated by collider searches, leaves a residual 2.51 x 10^56 times too large, and changing the normalisation by a factor of sixteen moves the required scale by less than a factor of two.

papers.t: Retuning After Every Transition: Vacuum-Energy Jumps at the Grand-Unification, Electroweak, and QCD Epochs
papers.r: Each cosmic phase transition shifts the vacuum energy by roughly the fourth power of its temperature: relative to the observed density of 2.52 x 10^-47 GeV^4, the electroweak jump spoils a prior cancellation by 54.6 decimal digits and the QCD jump, the last of the three, by 43.3 digits, so the present small density cannot have been arranged before a cosmic time of about 4.4 x 10^-5 seconds unless a mechanism tracks e

papers.t: How Much Room Above the Observed Value? A Reconstruction of the Galaxy-Formation Bound on the Vacuum Density
papers.r: Reconstructing the galaxy-formation bound with stated assumptions (peaks growing in proportion to the scale factor from equality at z = 3400, vacuum domination before collapse excluded), peak contrasts at equality from 0.001 to 0.03 cap the vacuum density at between 18 and 488,000 times the observed value, with the reference peak of 0.003 giving a cap of about 488 times the observed density.

classes.title: Torsion and Bounce Extensions

papers.t: How Long Does a Torsion Bounce Accelerate? Duration and Expansion of the Accelerating Window as a Function of Equation of State
papers.r: For dust the accelerating window opens at a density fraction r = 0.250 of the bounce density and lasts 2.309 bounce timescales in total across both branches, accumulating 0.462 e-folds of expansion on the expanding side. For radiation the duration is 1.414 bounce timescales. For stiff matter the window opens only at r = 0.400, lasts 0.816 bounce timescales, and accumulates 0.153 e-folds on the expanding side.

papers.t: The Temperature at a Spin-Driven Bounce: Margins Against the Nucleosynthesis and Quark-Hadron Scales
papers.r: The neutrino threshold corresponds to kT = 1.415e+03 MeV, which lies 3.2 orders of magnitude from the nucleosynthesis scale on the side recorded in the results file. The electron threshold corresponds to 3.200e+06 MeV, standing 6.5 orders of magnitude above the 1 MeV nucleosynthesis landmark. The neutron threshold corresponds to 1.372e+08 MeV, standing 6.0 orders of magnitude above the 150 MeV quark-hadron landmark.

papers.t: The Exponent Race in a Contracting Universe: For Which Equations of State Does Matter Catch the Torsion Term?
papers.r: The critical equation of state is w = 1.0: at exactly stiff matter the torsion-to-matter ratio remains at its normalised value 1.0e-06 at every scale factor, as the script verifies. Below the critical value, crossing is guaranteed and its location is computed.

papers.t: Entropy per Baryon Across a Torsion Bounce: The Size of the Adiabatic Violation in the Effective Description
papers.r: The net fractional change in comoving entropy across the bounce is 0.0 at a peak density ratio of unity: in this effective description the entropy that leaves the bounce equals the entropy that entered, exactly, because the correction is a function of density alone and the trajectory retraces its densities. The transient deviation during the crossing is a different matter.

papers.t: A Generalised Torsion Coupling: The Window Between a Bounce Above the Nucleosynthesis Density and Below the Planck Density
papers.r: For an electron fluid the allowed coupling range runs from beta = 2.787e-46, set by the Planck ceiling, to beta = 1.048e+26, set by the nucleosynthesis floor at density 1.524e+08 kg/m^3: a window 71.6 orders of magnitude wide. For a neutron fluid the range runs from 9.422e-40 to 3.544e+32, a window 71.6 orders of magnitude wide.

papers.t: The Contraction Budget for the Horizon Problem: E-Folds of Contraction Required in Matter and Stiff Bounces Compared
papers.r: A matter-like contraction must run for 128.9 e-folds of scale-factor decrease to shrink the comoving Hubble radius by the target factor of 10^28, during which the density grows by a factor of ten to the power 168.0. A radiation-like contraction needs 64.5 e-folds. A stiff contraction needs only 32.2 e-folds, with a density growth of ten to the power 84.0.

papers.t: The Minimum Scale Factor of a Spin-Driven Bounce as a Function of Spin Alignment, and the Alignment Below Which No Bounce Occurs Above the Planck Length
papers.r: Reducing the alignment to f = 0.1 raises the bounce density by a factor of one hundred and changes the minimum scale factor, relative to the fully aligned case, by the factor 4.64 recorded in the results file; at f = 0.01 the corresponding scale-factor ratio is 21.54.

papers.t: Counting Mixmaster Epochs Before a Torsion Bounce: How Much Bianchi IX Chaos Fits Above the Bounce Density
papers.r: The simulated mean logarithmic density gain per era is 1.387. Between nuclear saturation density and the neutron spin threshold there is room for 38.7 eras; between the nucleosynthesis density scale and the neutron threshold, 54.4 eras. Against the electron threshold the counts are 27.8 eras from nuclear density and 43.5 eras from the nucleosynthesis scale.

papers.t: Where Focusing Fails: The Density and Time Interval of Raychaudhuri Defocusing Around a Torsion Bounce
papers.r: For dust, focusing fails above a density ratio of 0.250, and the defocusing interval lasts 2.308 bounce timescales across both branches. For radiation the interval lasts 1.413 bounce timescales. For stiff matter the critical ratio rises to 0.400.

papers.t: Scalar Perturbations Through a Torsion Bounce: Which Wavelengths Emerge Unchanged and Which Are Processed
papers.r: At one tenth of the bounce wavenumber the amplification factor is 0.768: long-wavelength modes cross with an order-unity rescaling, neither preserved exactly nor destroyed. At the bounce wavenumber the factor is 0.705.

papers.t: Shear Cannot Be Outrun by Spin: The Constant Ratio of Anisotropy to Torsion Energy in a Contracting Bianchi I Universe
papers.r: The numerical check confirms the analytic expectation: with the spin density chosen for equality at unit scale factor, the ratio of the spin term to the shear term equals unity at every sampled scale factor, from a = 1 down to a = 10^-6, and the script records the ratio as constant (True).

papers.t: The Sound Speed of the Effective Spin Fluid: Where the Squared Sound Speed Changes Sign and What It Costs Perturbations
papers.r: For a radiation-like component the numerator of the squared sound speed vanishes at r = 0.100, and the quantity is negative over a fraction 0.400 of the density range up to the bounce. For stiff matter the zero sits at r = 0.167.

papers.t: The Shift of the Scalar Spectral Index Produced by a Torsion-Dominated Phase: Magnitude Against the Planck Uncertainty
papers.r: The shift reaches the Planck uncertainty at a density ratio of only r = 4.196e-03: a mode exiting the horizon when the density is a few parts in a thousand of the bounce density already carries, in this model, a tilt displacement of one standard deviation. At r = 0.01 the shift is 0.0100; at r = 0.1 it is 0.1026; at r = 0.5 it is 0.5858, which is 139.5 times the Planck uncertainty of 0.0042.

papers.t: Spin Cancellation Between Species: How Precisely Must Opposing Spin Populations Balance to Postpone a Bounce by a Given Factor?
papers.r: An imbalance of one part in a hundred between the opposing populations postpones the bounce by a factor of 1.000e+04 in density. An imbalance of one part in ten thousand postpones it by 1.000e+08. Inverted, the requirement is severe: postponement by a factor of 10 needs the populations balanced to an imbalance of 0.316; by a factor of 100, to 0.100; and by a factor of a million, to 1.000e-03.

papers.t: The Spin-Density Threshold of an Einstein-Cartan Bounce: Critical Densities for Electron, Nucleon and Neutrino Fluids
papers.r: For an electron fluid the threshold mass density is 1.598e+34 kg/m^3. For a neutron fluid it is 5.403e+40 kg/m^3, larger by a factor of 3.381e+06, which is the square of the neutron-to-electron mass ratio, as the analytic form requires. A neutrino fluid of particle mass 0.1 eV reaches threshold at only 6.118e+20 kg/m^3.

papers.t: Tensor Modes Across a Torsion Bounce: Transmission Factors for Gravitational Waves as a Function of Wavenumber
papers.r: At one tenth of the bounce wavenumber the transmission factor is 3.776: long-wavelength modes are amplified, not merely transmitted, because the anti-friction of the contracting branch pumps modes whose period is long compared with the bounce duration, and the expansion afterwards does not fully undo that pumping within the integration window.

papers.t: Which Species Turns Around First? Threshold Crossing Order in a Cooling, Contracting Mixture of Neutrinos, Electrons and Nucleons
papers.r: The crossing order is by mass, lightest first. The neutrino component crosses at an equivalent radiation temperature of 1.642e+13 K, the electron component at 3.712e+16 K, and the neutron component at 1.592e+18 K.

homework.q: Take the paper “How Long Does a Torsion Bounce Accelerate? Duration and Expansion of the Accelerating Window as a Function of Equation of State”. Its stated result is: For dust the accelerating window opens at a density fraction r = 0.250 of the bounce density and lasts 2.309 bounce timescales in total across both branches, accumulating 0.462 e-folds of expansion on the expanding side. For radiation the duration is 1.414 bounce timescales. (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong.
homework.worked: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

classes.title: The CMB Line

papers.t: The Chance Probability of the Quadrupole-Octopole Alignment: A Monte Carlo Census of Random Axes
papers.r: The quadrupole and octopole of the microwave sky define preferred axes, and the two axes are reported to lie within roughly ten degrees of each other, a coincidence often cited as evidence against statistical isotropy.

papers.t: How Far Should a Preferred Axis Wander? Fisher Geometry of Axis Estimation and the Consistency of Axes Reported at Different Multipole Ranges
papers.r: Preferred axes are reported from different multipole ranges, different statistics, and different experiments, and their directions never quite agree; the disagreements are then argued over as though an axis were a point rather than an estimate. This paper computes how much wander an axis estimate should show, from Fisher geometry on the sphere.

papers.t: Beyond the Average: Azimuthal Fourier Modes About a Preferred Axis as a Test of Axisymmetry, and the Leakage Budget of a Localised Spot
papers.r: The azimuthal average throws away everything about a ring except its mean, including the information that distinguishes a true ring from an arc or a spot. This paper develops the complementary statistic, the azimuthal Fourier decomposition at fixed polar angle, and computes its discriminating power at the Cold Spot's latitude.

papers.t: Must the Cold Spot Be Compensated? Integrated Temperature Flux of the Spot's Profile and the Ring Amplitude Its Surroundings Allow
papers.r: A primordial cold spot is not just a depression; integrated over a wide enough disc, its temperature flux must nearly vanish, because the feature is built from multipoles of order two and above whose spherical integrals are zero. This paper computes the compensation bookkeeping for the Cold Spot's published core profile.

papers.t: How Cold Can a Supervoid Make the Microwave Sky? An Integrated Sachs-Wolfe Bound Against the Cold Spot's Central Depth
papers.r: The Cold Spot, a cold region roughly ten degrees across centred near galactic coordinates (207.8 degrees, -56.3 degrees), has a published central depth near -150 microK, and the large underdensity reported in its direction has often been named as its cause through the integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect.

papers.t: Recovering a Dipolar Modulation from a Masked Sky: Bias and Variance of the Hemispherical Power Asymmetry Estimator at Planck Amplitude
papers.r: Planck's isotropy analyses report a dipolar modulation of the low-multipole sky, an amplitude of about 0.07 in the local power, equivalent to a hemispherical power asymmetry. This paper asks how faithfully the standard hemispherical estimator recovers such a modulation, using three hundred synthetic skies at each of four injected amplitudes.

papers.t: Could a Foreground Residual Fake the Cold Spot? The Required Residual Amplitude at 143 Gigahertz and Its Frequency Fingerprint
papers.r: A foreground residual cold enough to imitate the Cold Spot would betray itself by its spectrum, because galactic emission is not blackbody. This paper computes the fingerprint. A dust-like residual producing -150 microK at 143 gigahertz would produce -303.2 microK at 217 gigahertz and -103.2 microK at 100 gigahertz; a synchrotron-like residual would reach -341.3 microK at 100 gigahertz; a free-free-like residual woul

papers.t: The Look-Elsewhere Ledger: A Trials-Factor Accounting for the Large-Angle Anomaly Catalogue as a Whole
papers.r: The large-angle anomalies are usually argued one at a time, each with its own percentile, and the catalogue as a whole is then described as either damning or negligible according to taste. This paper does the catalogue-level arithmetic.

papers.t: The Low Quadrupole in Numbers: Cosmic-Variance Tail Probability of the Observed Quadrupole Power and What Would Change It
papers.r: The observed quadrupole power of the microwave sky, D2 = 225.9 microK squared in Planck PR3 bookkeeping, sits well below the value the best-fit cosmological model leads one to expect, and the size of that shortfall is often described in words rather than numbers. This paper computes the exact cosmic-variance tail probability.

papers.t: Mask Bias in Annulus Means: How Much a Galactic Cut Can Move an Azimuthal Average, Computed on Synthetic Skies
papers.r: Every azimuthal-average analysis of the real microwave sky is performed through a galactic mask, and the mask is not innocent: in the rotated frame of a chosen axis the galactic band cuts each annulus unevenly, removing different azimuths at different latitudes. This paper measures what that does to annulus means, using six hundred synthetic Gaussian skies analysed with and without a Planck-like galactic band.

papers.t: Multipole Vectors and the Area Statistic: How Often Random Skies Produce Octopole Planarity and Quadrupole-Octopole Vector Alignments
papers.r: The octopole of the microwave sky is described as planar, its multipole vectors clustered so that their area vectors nearly coincide, and its orientation is tied to the quadrupole's in the alignment discussions. This paper computes how often isotropic skies produce area-vector statistics as extreme as the values quoted for the real sky.

papers.t: Parity Asymmetry at Low Multipoles: The Strongest Odd-Even Imbalance Cosmic Variance Permits, and Where the Reported Effect Sits Within It
papers.r: Point-parity asymmetry, an excess of power in odd multipoles over even ones at large angles, has been reported in the microwave sky at up to roughly three-sigma significance in some treatments. This paper computes the exact null behaviour of the standard parity ratio by Monte Carlo over the known chi-square distribution of power estimates.

papers.t: A Polarisation Test to Separate a Primordial Cold Spot from a Void Imprint: Predicted E-Mode Signatures and the Sensitivity a Decisive Measurement Requires
papers.r: Temperature alone cannot finally separate a primordial Cold Spot from one cast by a late-time void, because both write in the same channel. Polarisation can, in principle: a primordial adiabatic feature carries the temperature-polarisation correlation imprint of the acoustic era, while an integrated Sachs-Wolfe imprint does not. This paper designs that test quantitatively.

papers.t: Ring or Spot? The Azimuthal Smearing Factor That Separates a Latitude Ring from a Localised Cold Spot, and the Signal Each Leaves in Annulus Means
papers.r: Two rival accounts of the Cold Spot predict different things in the azimuthal average about the reported preferred axis: a profile in which the spot is one point on a cold ring at polar angle 123.40 degrees predicts an annulus mean of -17.7 microK at that latitude at the registered amplitude cap, while a localised spot predicts only the small residue left when a compact feature is smeared around a full ring.

papers.t: The Missing Large-Angle Correlation: Computing S1/2 from a Sachs-Wolfe Spectrum and Placing the Observed Deficit on a Cosmic-Variance Scale
papers.r: The two-point correlation function of the microwave sky nearly vanishes at separations above sixty degrees, a feature summarised by the statistic S1/2, whose observed value near 1300 microK to the fourth power sits far below ensemble expectations.

papers.t: The Noise Floor of an Azimuthal-Average Template Fit: Minimum Detectable Amplitude for a Fixed Low-Multipole Profile on the Planck Sky
papers.r: A fixed low-multipole profile fitted to azimuthal averages about a chosen axis returns one number, an amplitude, and that number is only as informative as the scatter of the same fit on skies with no profile present.

papers.t: At What Scale Is the Cold Spot? Wavelet Response of a Compensated Spot Across Scales and the Scale-Selection Bias in Its Reported Significance
papers.r: The Cold Spot was found by a wavelet, and wavelets are used at many scales: the spherical Mexican hat's response to the spot peaks at a particular scale, and the spot's reported significance has always been quoted at the scale where it looks largest. This paper computes the response curve and prices the selection.

homework.q: Take the paper “The Chance Probability of the Quadrupole-Octopole Alignment: A Monte Carlo Census of Random Axes”. Its stated result is: The quadrupole and octopole of the microwave sky define preferred axes, and the two axes are reported to lie within roughly ten degrees of each other, a coincidence often cited as evidence against statistical isotropy. (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong.

classes.title: The Fifth Coordinate and the Transit Law

papers.t: How Close Can Destinations Sit? Minimum Phase Separation for Reliable Addressing
papers.r: Destinations that sit too close together on the phase circle will be confused with one another. This paper derives the minimum separation for reliable addressing. With Gaussian arrival error of standard deviation sigma and nearest-neighbour decisions, keeping the misdelivery probability at or below one in a million requires a separation of at least 2 sigma x 4.7534.

papers.t: The Causality Dwell Bound: Minimum Transit Time for Displacement Through a Fifth Coordinate
papers.r: A transit that changes ordinary position as well as phase invites an immediate causality question: what stops the effective speed from exceeding the speed of light? This paper derives the answer as a minimum dwell time.

papers.t: What Clocks Already Exclude: A Coupling Bound for the Fifth Coordinate from Optical-Clock Sensitivity
papers.r: If the fifth coordinate couples to ordinary matter, precision clocks should notice. This paper converts the sensitivity of modern optical-clock comparisons into a bound on that coupling. Assuming an advance Dchi of the phase shifts a clock's fractional frequency by g_chi Dchi, and taking the unexplained-shift sensitivity as 1e-18, the coupling is bounded by g_chi <= 1.592e-19 per radian for a full turn and g_chi <= 1

papers.t: How Long Must a Phase Remember Itself? Coherence-Time Requirements for Controlled Transit
papers.r: A controlled transit is a coherent process: the phase must mean the same thing at arrival as it did at departure. This paper derives the coherence-time requirement that follows from a transit's duration. With fidelity F = exp(-T_tr/T2), a sixty-second chamber transit retains fidelity 0.3679 if the coherence time is also sixty seconds, 0.9835 if coherence lasts an hour, and 0.9993 if it lasts a day.

papers.t: How Large Can the Circle Be? A Radius Bound for the Fifth Coordinate from Its Excitation Gap
papers.r: A phase that lives on a circle has a size, and the size has a spectrum. This paper derives the relation between the circle radius R of the fifth coordinate and the energy gap to its first excitation, E_1 = hbar c / R, and converts physical requirements into bounds on R.

papers.t: Arriving Within Tolerance: Transit Success Probability Under Advance-Rate Dispersion
papers.r: A transit that aims at a phase and arrives at a neighbouring one has not failed loudly; it has failed by a small angle, which is worse. This paper computes the probability of arriving within tolerance when the advance rate varies across a payload.

papers.t: The Price of a Turn: Energy and Power for Phase Transit of Macroscopic Payloads
papers.r: What would it cost, energetically, to advance the phase of a macroscopic payload through one full turn? This paper evaluates a stated drive model in which the energy per turn for mass M completed in time T is E = E_ref M (1 s/T)^2 with E_ref = 4.494e+05 J per kilogram at a one-second turn.

papers.t: Spending the Same Budget a Thousand Times: Phase Error Accumulation Over Repeated Transits
papers.r: A vehicle that transits repeatedly does not get a fresh phase error budget on each journey; it spends from the same account. This paper derives how per-pass errors accumulate. Independent random errors of sigma_1 per pass grow as sigma_1 sqrt(N) over N passes, while a systematic bias b grows as bN.

papers.t: The Address Is Cheap: Information Content and Thermodynamic Floor of a Phase Destination
papers.r: A phase coordinate is also an address space. This paper counts it. At a readout resolution of 0.0667 rad, one turn holds 94.2 distinguishable addresses, carrying 6.558 bits; four turns of address depth hold 7.874e+07 addresses and 26.231 bits.

papers.t: Addresses Decay: A Diffusion Bound on the Holding Time of a Phase Destination
papers.r: A phase left alone does not stay put; coupled to any environment, it diffuses. This paper derives the holding requirement that follows. With phase diffusion constant D, free diffusion exhausts the 0.0667 rad budget in 2224 s at D = 1e-6 rad^2/s, in 2.224e+05 s at D = 1e-8, and in 2.224e+07 s at D = 1e-10.

papers.t: The Phase-Winding Energy Ladder: Quadratic Cost of Transit in a Fifth Coordinate
papers.r: Transit in a fifth coordinate that is an angular phase chi requires the phase to advance, and advancing it costs energy. This paper derives the resulting energy ladder from a stated kinetic form, E(n) = E1 n^2 for winding number n, with the unit step fixed at E1 = 0.01 eV, and tabulates which windings a given energy budget can buy.

papers.t: Clocks at Different Heights: The Gravitational Redshift Correction to Transit Timing
papers.r: Clocks at different heights run at different rates, and a timed transit between heights inherits the difference. This paper computes the gravitational redshift correction to transit timing for endpoints separated vertically in Earth's field. The fractional rate difference is 1.093e-16 for one metre, 4.112e-11 for a 400 km orbit, and 5.292e-10 at navigation-satellite altitude.

papers.t: Resonance Is a Bargain with Terms: Enhancement, Bandwidth and Ring-Up in Phase Driving
papers.r: Driving a phase coordinate resonantly multiplies a weak drive by the quality factor Q, at the price of bandwidth. This paper computes the trade for a damped-oscillator model of the phase response. At Q = 100 the on-resonance enhancement is 100, but a detuning of 1 percent cuts the response to 44.72; at Q = 1000 a detuning of only 0.1 percent already cuts the response to 447.21, and the fractional bandwidth is 0.001.

papers.t: The Rotating Frame Fights Back: Sagnac Phase Corrections for Transit on Earth
papers.r: Rotation writes itself into any phase measured around a loop, and transit paths on a rotating planet are loops whether their designers draw them that way or not. This paper computes the Sagnac-type timing and phase offsets for transit paths on Earth.

papers.t: Thermal Phase Noise and the Temperature Ceiling for Reliable Fifth-Coordinate Readout
papers.r: Thermal agitation blurs any coordinate held in a potential, and the phase coordinate is no exception. This paper models the phase as held by a harmonic stiffness kappa = 4.142e-17 J per rad^2, calibrated so the thermal phase spread is 0.01 rad at 300 K, and computes the temperature ceiling for reliable readout.

papers.t: A Timing Floor for Phase Transit: Duration Bounds from the Energy-Time Uncertainty Relation
papers.r: How fast can a phase coordinate be advanced? This paper derives a floor on transit duration from the energy-time uncertainty relation, dt >= hbar/(2 dE), applied to a fifth coordinate whose advance Dchi must be resolved against an available energy spread dE.

papers.t: Not Free: Three Computed Floors Refuting the Claim of Zero-Energy Phase Transit
papers.r: A claim circulates in popular discussions of extra coordinates: because the fifth coordinate is 'only a phase', advancing it costs no energy and transit along it is free. This paper states the claim plainly and refutes it with three independent floors, each computed. Recording the arrival address of 6.558 bits at 300 K costs at least 1.883e-20 J by the Landauer limit.

homework.q: Take the paper “How Close Can Destinations Sit? Minimum Phase Separation for Reliable Addressing”. Its stated result is: Destinations that sit too close together on the phase circle will be confused with one another. This paper derives the minimum separation for reliable addressing. (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong.

professor.name: Professor Min-Ho Yoon
professor.personality: A unhurried and exact teacher of Cosmology who slows down exactly where the textbooks speed up. He motto, written on the board in week one and never erased: the subject is learnable, and so are you.

classes.title: Machine Designs

papers.t: A Bounce-Regime Impact Cushion: Crush Stroke and Peak Load for a Landing Pad Using Torsion Pressure Near the Bounce
papers.r: The device is a landing cushion pad, sized here for a two-tonne descending vehicle, built around a crush core of spin-polarised material whose resistance rises steeply as it is compressed, in the manner that torsion pressure rises as matter approaches a bounce rather than a singularity, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script.

papers.t: A Bounce-Assisted Lunar Lander: Terminal Descent Propellant Saving from a Torsion Cushion Stage
papers.r: The device is a lunar lander of fifteen hundred kilograms dry mass whose final descent segment, from fifteen metres at a stated vertical speed, is absorbed by a torsion cushion stage of the kind characterised in the companion cushion study, instead of by propulsive braking, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script.

papers.t: A Bounce Press for Materials Densification: Peak Pressure and Work Input for a Torsion-Assisted Compaction Cycle
papers.r: The device is a compaction press whose die contains a spin-polarised backing element, so that as the compact's density climbs, the torsion pressure of the aligned backing rises in support of the ram and contributes an increasing share of the densification work, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script.

papers.t: A Density-Capped Confinement Vessel: Sizing a Magnetic Bottle Whose Operating Point Sits Below the Aldred Density by Construction
papers.r: The device is a toroidal magnetic confinement vessel, scanned over minor radius, operating a deuterium-tritium plasma at fifteen kiloelectronvolts and a stated density of ten to the twentieth particles per cubic metre, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script.

papers.t: A Spin-Polarised Shield Panel: Radiation Attenuation and Mass Trade for Crewed Transit Vehicles
papers.r: The device is a hull panel of hydrogen-rich polymer whose hydrogen nuclei are maintained in a spin-polarised state, adding a stated torsion-coupled increment to the panel's mass attenuation coefficient for the cosmic-ray dose proxy used in this study, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script.

papers.t: A Spin-Polarised Propellant Thruster: Thrust and Specific Impulse from Torsion-Assisted Exhaust Expansion
papers.r: The device is a magnetic-nozzle thruster fed with hydrogen whose nuclei are spin-polarised before ionisation, so that the expansion of the exhaust through the nozzle is assisted by the torsion coupling of the aligned spin population, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script. The unpolarised specific impulse is 458.9 s.

papers.t: A Shear-Capped Acceleration Stage: Gradient Limits for a Compact Linear Accelerator Set by the Aldred Shear Bound
papers.r: The device is a ten-metre copper accelerating stage intended to add a stated energy increment to a charged-particle beam, with its gradient chosen not by optimism but by an explicit shear criterion applied to the electromagnetic stress in the cavity walls, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script.

papers.t: An Aldred Shear Densitometer: A Non-Contact Sensor Reading Density Against the Shear Bound
papers.r: The device is a densitometer whose sensing element is a small spin-polarised torsional resonator mounted outside the vessel wall, its resonant frequency shifting, under the stated coupling model, in proportion to the density of the material within its sensing volume, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script.

papers.t: A Shear Relief Valve for High-Density Plasma Conduits: Opening Pressure Set by the Aldred Shear Bound
papers.r: The device is a diaphragm relief valve for a high-density plasma conduit, whose opening pressure is set by applying a stated small fraction of the Aldred shear bound to the diaphragm area and balancing it against a spring preload, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script.

papers.t: A Torsion-Balanced Clock: Rate Stability of a Polarised Torsion Pendulum as a Transit Timing Reference
papers.r: The device is a torsion pendulum clock: a disc suspended on a fine fibre, oscillating in twist, with the disc material spin-polarised so that its torsion constant carries a stated contribution from the aligned spin population, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script.

papers.t: A Torsion-Coupled Flywheel: Energy Storage in a Spin-Polarised Rotor Limited by Shear at the Aldred Density
papers.r: The device studied here is a solid cylindrical steel rotor, 0.60 m in diameter and 0.40 m long, whose material is taken to be spin-polarised so that torsion in the Einstein-Cartan sense supplies an additional internal pressure opposing the centrifugal hoop stress, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script.

papers.t: A Torsion Gyroscope: Drift Budget for an Inertial Reference Unit Using a Spin-Polarised Rotor
papers.r: The device is a single-axis gyroscope whose rotor is spin-polarised, so that the torsion field of the rotor's own aligned spin population stiffens its response to disturbance torques that would otherwise appear as drift, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script. The rotor stores 3.208 kg m^2/s of angular momentum.

papers.t: A Fifth-Coordinate Timing Beacon: Clock Synchronisation Across a Transit Link and Its Error Budget
papers.r: The device is a timing beacon pair, one at each end of an Earth-Moon baseline, exchanging pulses through a fifth-coordinate transit path and disciplining two atomic clocks to a common epoch, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script. At transit parameter 1.0 the one-way signal time over the Earth-Moon baseline is 1.6836 s.

papers.t: A Transit Gate Ring: Power Scaling and Thermal Load for a Fifth-Coordinate Portal of Stated Aperture
papers.r: The device is a circular gate ring, scanned from half a metre to five metres in aperture radius, that sustains the boundary conditions for a fifth-coordinate transit at a stated operating parameter, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script.

papers.t: Closed-Loop Life Support for a Fifth-Coordinate Transit Capsule: Consumables Budget Across Crossing Durations
papers.r: The device is the closed-loop life-support system of a four-person transit capsule designed for fifth-coordinate crossings, sized not for the crossing itself, which occupies seconds, but for the gate dwell, delay, and contingency durations that surround it, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script.

papers.t: A Fifth-Coordinate Transit Pod: Timing and Energy Budget for an Earth-Moon Crossing Under the Transit Law
papers.r: The device is a crewed transit pod of one to five tonnes that crosses between Earth and Moon not by thrust along the ordinary path but by a brief excursion through a fifth coordinate, entering and leaving ordinary space at powered gate structures at each end, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script.

papers.t: A Vacuum Dissolution Cell: Extractable Power from the Surviving Count After Vacuum Contributions Dissolve
papers.r: The device is a sealed resonant cell, one cubic metre in the reference size, intended to couple cyclically to the surviving vacuum contribution and convert a stated small fraction of each cycle's coupled energy into electrical power, derived from stated assumptions and computed throughout by the accompanying script.
