homework.q: Take the paper “1982-83 Reconstructed: Growth Interval, Peak Amplitude and the Thermocline Budget of a Poorly Observed Event”. Its stated result is: Headline result: event82 growth rate per month event82 = 0.2131; event82 linear rate k per month event82 = 0.275; event82 efolding months event82 = 4.693; event82 inferred displacement m event82 = 51.19; event82 subsurface warming k event82 = 5.119; event82 recognition delay months event82 = 5 Opera (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong.
homework.worked: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

professor.name: Professor Natalia Morales
professor.personality: A gentle and rigorous teacher of Geophysics who reads the primary source aloud before trusting any summary of it. Examinations in her room are open-book, because she is testing thinking, not storage.
professor.greeting: In, in. Geophysics waits for no one, and neither do we.

professor.name: Professor Stefan Nowak
professor.personality: Crisp to the point of music; a proof in his room is built like a bridge, in the open, one honest span at a time. 'Almost rigorous' is his only insult, and he has used it twice in a decade.
professor.greeting: We begin from definitions. Everything else is negotiation.

papers.t: Crossing Times, Time Gains and Station-Keeping in a Wormhole Shortcut
papers.r: A wormhole whose mouths sit one astronomical unit apart replaces an external light-travel time of 499.0 seconds with a through-throat crossing of 3.336e-04 seconds at one tenth of light speed over an assumed ten-kilometre internal path, a gain of 1.50e+06. For mouths separated by the distance to Proxima Centauri the external signal time is 1.379e+08 seconds and the gain rises to 4.13e+11.

papers.t: Free Core Nutation: Inferring Core Flattening from the Resonance Period
papers.r: This paper computes free core nutation period inference from stated assumptions and deposits the full computation. Headline results: observed resonance period 430 sidereal days; effective core ellipticity required 0.0188; ellipticity from boundary shape alone 0.0064; period a shape-only model would give 1269 days; share that compliance and coupling must supply 66 percent.

papers.t: Frequency Drift in Repeating Bursts as a Dispersion-Slope Test
papers.r: Mimicking a typical repeater drift of minus twenty megahertz per millisecond would require a dispersion error of about 1.3 units, against a measurement precision near a hundredth of a unit and observed burst-to-burst dispersion stability at the same level, so observed drifts are conclusively source or lensing physics.

papers.t: Keeping Two Wormhole Mouths Apart: Mutual Tides, Orbital Periods and Minimum Separation
papers.r: A wormhole mouth is not a weightless doorway: its gravitational mass parameter is set by its radius, and for a ten-metre throat that parameter is 6.73e+27 kilograms, of planetary order. Two such mouths attract, orbit and tidally stress anything between them.

papers.t: Lunar Recession and the Lengthening Day: An Angular-Momentum Consistency Check
papers.r: This paper computes lunar recession rate consistency check from stated assumptions and deposits the full computation. Headline results: predicted lengthening from the recession 2.11 ms per century; long-term eclipse average 1.7 ms per century; residual to be supplied by rebound and coupling 0.41 ms per century; tidal torque 4.53e+16 N m.

papers.t: Natario's Zero-Expansion Warp Drive: Does Removing Expansion Remove the Negative Energy?
papers.r: Natario's warp construction sets the expansion of the Eulerian flow to zero identically, so the bubble transports its contents without the volume expansion and contraction that define Alcubierre's original. It is natural to hope the negative energy was tied to the expansion and left with it.

papers.t: Satellite Geodesy J2 Recovered from Hydrostatic Flattening and the Density Profile
papers.r: This paper computes satellite geodesy j2 from density from stated assumptions and deposits the full computation. Headline results: J2 from the Clairaut relation 1.08140e-03; satellite J2 1.08263e-03; residual -0.11 percent; Radau polar moment factor 0.331; accepted polar moment factor 0.331. The study is simulated and computed, not measured, and every number in the paper is produced by the deposited compute.py.

papers.t: Scintillation Bandwidth Scaling for Dispersed Radio Sources
papers.r: Scintillation bandwidths collapse from hundreds of megahertz for nearby low-dispersion sources to tens of kilohertz for dispersion-500 bursts at 600 MHz, below the channel widths of the surveys that detect them. The absence of visible scintillation in most burst spectra is therefore primarily an instrumental fact, and emission-region inferences drawn from it require a resolution correction of the size computed here.

papers.t: Stability Condition for a Two-Horizon Dumb Hole Derived from Surface-Gravity Ordering
papers.r: Computed headline values for this analogue system are: trt_mid_ms = 66.7, gain_mid = 5.09, gain_wide = 5.31. The study is simulated and computed from stated assumptions and published experimental scales, not measured, and every value is reproducible from the deposited calculation script and results file.

papers.t: Superradiant Amplification Gain in a Rotating Absorbing Flow Computed from Mode Frequencies
papers.r: Computed headline values for this analogue system are: thresh_m1_Om10_Hz = 1.59, gain_ex = 1.150, gain_pct = 15.0. The study is simulated and computed from stated assumptions and published experimental scales, not measured, and every value is reproducible from the deposited calculation script and results file.

papers.t: Surface Gravity Compared Across Four Analogue Platforms on a Common Footing
papers.r: Computed headline values for this analogue system are: T_BEC_nK = 0.58, T_He_uK = 0.1, T_fibre_K = 24.31, T_water_K = 2.83e-12, span_orders = 12.9. The study is simulated and computed from stated assumptions and published experimental scales, not measured, and every value is reproducible from the deposited calculation script and results file.

papers.t: The Casimir Effect as a Wormhole Source: Matching Density and the Total-Energy Shortfall
papers.r: The Casimir energy density between conducting plates grows as the inverse fourth power of their separation. To match the 4.82e+42 joules per cubic metre that a one-metre wormhole throat requires, the plates must stand 3.08e-18 metres apart, well inside the scale of atoms, where the ideal-conductor formula has long ceased to describe any real material.

papers.t: The Chandler Wobble Period as a Check on Terrestrial Elasticity
papers.r: This paper computes chandler wobble period check from stated assumptions and deposits the full computation. Headline results: rigid Euler period 304 days; observed Chandler period 433 days; lengthening factor 1.42; effective Love number inferred 0.28; independently measured Love number k2 0.30. The study is simulated and computed, not measured, and every number in the paper is produced by the deposited compute.py.

papers.t: The Cumulative Energy Budget of a Repeating Fast Radio Burst
papers.r: Three hundred bursts from an FRB 121102-class repeater total under ten to the forty-second ergs in radio energy, consuming about a ten-thousandth of a magnetar reservoir at one percent efficiency and supporting tens of millennia of activity. Repetition is energetically affordable for magnetars, excludes only weak-field reservoirs, and makes radio efficiency the decisive unknown in repeater source models.

papers.t: The Flare-Out Condition at a Wormhole Throat Tested Against a Maximum Shear Rate
papers.r: A traversable throat must flare outward, and flaring is a statement about how the geometry shears as one moves away from the throat. For the shape function b of r equals r nought squared over r, whose slope at the throat is minus one, the orthonormal shear scale at the throat is about 3.00e+08 per second for a one-metre throat, a ratio of 7.43e-17 to the maximum shear rate of 4.04e+24 per second set by spin-torsion p

papers.t: The Krasnikov Tube: Energy Cost of a Permanent Faster-Than-Light Corridor
papers.r: A Krasnikov tube is a corridor of modified spacetime, laid down by a traveller moving near light speed, along which the return journey can be made arbitrarily fast. Integrating the wall energy density over a cylindrical shell for a tube one light-year long gives 2.86e+58 joules for a one-metre radius, 2.86e+58 joules for ten metres, the latter equal to 1.60e+11 solar mass-energies, with a wall density of 4.82e+40 jou

papers.t: The Luminosity Cutoff of the Fast Radio Burst Population
papers.r: A fluence-limited survey detects bursts above ten to the fortieth ergs at redshift 0.5 and several times higher at redshift 1, with the brightest catalogue events near ten to the forty-second ergs — affordable for magnetar reservoirs and far below any fundamental ceiling, so the population's apparent top end is presently a selection effect and the physical cutoff, if one exists, lies above the observed range.

papers.t: The Minimum Exotic Mass of a One-Metre Wormhole Throat
papers.r: Integrating the exotic matter of a Morris-Thorne throat gives a total that scales linearly with the throat radius. For a one-metre throat the integral evaluates to 1.35e+27 kilograms of negative mass, 0.71 Jupiter masses, or 2.25e+02 Earth masses; its energy equivalent equals what the Sun radiates in 1.00e+10 years.

papers.t: The Scattering Budget of Fast Radio Bursts Against Dispersion Measure
papers.r: Evaluated across the observed dispersion range, the Galactic scattering relation rises from negligible broadening at dispersion 100 to tens of milliseconds at dispersion 1000, with ten-millisecond broadening reached within the observed range and a fiftyfold penalty at 400 MHz.

papers.t: The Timing Stability Limit of Millisecond Pulsars
papers.r: A 5.76-millisecond pulsar timed at 65 nanoseconds over fifteen years accumulates of order ten to the eleventh counted rotations, holds phase to about a part in ten to the fifth of a turn, and excludes steady fractional frequency drifts at the ten-to-the-minus-sixteen level — performance that leaves no room for anomalous steady torques of the kind a noisy bounce variant might have produced.

papers.t: The Total Exotic Energy of an Alcubierre Bubble at One Hundred Metres
papers.r: Integrating the energy density of an Alcubierre bubble of radius one hundred metres moving at light speed gives a total exotic energy of 1.01e+47 joules for a one-metre wall, equal to 5.64e-01 times the entire mass-energy of the Sun, or 5.91e+02 Jupiter masses in equivalent mass. Thinning the wall makes the requirement worse in direct proportion, and at a Planck-scale wall it reaches 1.01e+79 joules.

papers.t: Thermal Design of a Transition-Edge Sensor Bolometer Array: Conductance, Noise-Equivalent Power and Saturation Margin
papers.r: Computed design (SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED): phonon-noise-equivalent power per pixel 15.4 attowatt per root hertz; saturation power per pixel 8.44 pW; ratio of saturation power to the stated optical load 2.11 dimensionless; effective response time under electrothermal feedback 0.153 ms; electrothermal loop gain 28.1 dimensionless.

papers.t: Thermal Load Budget and Helium-3 Circulation Requirement for a Dilution Refrigerator Stage Reaching Ten Millikelvin
papers.r: Computed design (SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED): heat conducted down the supports 3.6 microwatt; heat conducted along the wiring loom 0.384 microwatt; radiative load from the still-temperature shield 2.32e-05 microwatt; total steady load on the mixing chamber 4.38 microwatt; helium-3 circulation needed to hold 10 mK under the full load 461 micromol per second.

papers.t: Throat Energy Density of a Morris-Thorne Wormhole Against a Maximum-Density Ceiling
papers.r: A static Morris-Thorne throat of radius one metre requires a negative energy density of 5.36e+25 kilograms per cubic metre in mass-equivalent units. A maximum density for fermionic matter of 9.72e+57 kilograms per cubic metre, set by spin-torsion repulsion on the neutron branch, lies 32.3 orders of magnitude above that requirement, so the ceiling does not exclude the throat: the two numbers are separated by a factor

papers.t: Tidal Accelerations at a Wormhole Throat and the Radius a Human Traveller Requires
papers.r: A human traveller two metres tall crossing a wormhole throat experiences tidal accelerations that scale as the inverse square of the throat radius. Using the Morris-Thorne tidal relations with an order-unity curvature coefficient appropriate to the zero-tidal-force shape family, a throat of one hundred metres imposes about 5.00e+03 times Earth gravity across the traveller's body, which no traveller could survive.

papers.t: Time Shift Between Wormhole Mouths and the Chronology Threshold
papers.r: Moving one mouth of a wormhole pair makes the mouths age at different rates, so the throat connects two moments as well as two places. A mouth carried at one tenth of light speed for one year returns with a time shift of 1.83 days relative to its twin; at half of light speed the shift is 48.9 days, and even at one hundredth of light speed it is 1.58e+03 seconds.

papers.t: A Fifty-Metre Millimetre-Wave Single Dish: Surface Accuracy, Ruze Efficiency and Beam Size Computed Across the Submillimetre Bands
papers.r: A 50 m single-dish telescope for millimetre and submillimetre astronomy is designed from the physics of its reflecting surface. With an actively controlled surface of 55 micrometres root-mean-square accuracy, the Ruze formula gives aperture efficiencies of 0.57 at 230 GHz, 0.40 at 345 GHz and 0.06 at 690 GHz, an effective area of 782 square metres and a gain of 0.28 K per Jy at 345 GHz.

papers.t: A Network of Axion Haloscopes: Scan Rate and Frequency Coverage Computed from the Cavity Conversion Equation
papers.r: A network of four axion haloscopes is designed from the scan-rate equation that governs the search for axion dark matter. Each instrument — an 8 T magnet, a 0.20 cubic metre cavity of loaded quality factor 80,000 and a quantum-limited receiver at 0.35 K system temperature — scans at 0.33 GHz per year at the benchmark coupling. Four instruments on adjacent bands cover 1 to 8 GHz in 5.3 years.

papers.t: A Network of Optical Lattice Clocks for Ultralight Dark Matter and Relativistic Geodesy: Coupling Reach Computed from Clock Instability
papers.r: Twelve optical lattice clocks, each with fractional instability 1e-16 per root second averaging to a 3e-19 floor, are designed as a correlated network. The 66 pairwise comparisons suppress uncorrelated clock noise, giving a detectable oscillating fractional-frequency amplitude of 3.69e-20 for an ultralight scalar field of mass 1e-17 eV over its 4.14e+08 second coherence time, corresponding under the stated field mode

papers.t: A Triangular Underground Gravitational-Wave Observatory with Ten-Kilometre Arms: Noise Budget and Binary-Neutron-Star Horizon Computed from First Principles
papers.r: A third-generation ground-based gravitational-wave observatory is designed as a triangle of three interferometers with 10 km arms, sited underground, and its performance is computed from an explicit noise model.

papers.t: A Twenty-Kilotonne Liquid Scintillator Detector: Energy Resolution and Reactor-Antineutrino Statistics Computed from Light Yield
papers.r: A spherical liquid scintillator neutrino detector of 20 kilotonnes is designed around one quantity: its light yield. At 1,200 photoelectrons per MeV, collected by 14,934 photomultipliers at 75 percent coverage of a vessel of radius 17.6 m, the computed energy resolution is 3.06 percent at 1 MeV, 1.94 percent at 3 MeV and 3.69 percent at 662 keV, including a stated 1 percent constant term.

papers.t: A Two-Hundred-Fifty-Six-Dish Array for 21-Centimetre Intensity Mapping: Thermal Noise and Baryon-Acoustic-Oscillation Significance Computed from the Survey Model
papers.r: An intensity-mapping array for the redshifted 21-centimetre line of neutral hydrogen is designed from its thermal-noise budget. Two hundred fifty-six 6 m dishes with 50 K system temperature, observing 400 to 800 MHz, survey 15,000 square degrees in four years, spending 119,593 seconds per pointing and reaching a brightness-temperature noise of 0.10 mK per megahertz channel per pointing.

papers.t: A Variability Timescale Floor for Quasars From Light Crossing and a Shear Ceiling
papers.r: The computation converts published quasar and active-galaxy source properties into density and shear units and compares them with a spin-torsion density ceiling of 9.718e+57 kg/m3 and a derived shear ceiling of 4.037e+24 per second.

papers.t: An Aperture-Synthesis Radio Array Sized from Receiver Noise and Survey Speed: A Computed Design
papers.r: This paper presents a computed design for a ground-based aperture-synthesis radio observatory of 214 parabolic antennas of 18 m diameter, and derives its performance from receiver noise, collecting area and baseline geometry rather than adopting the figures of any existing instrument.

papers.t: Broad-Line Region Densities From the Ionisation Parameter Against a Density Ceiling
papers.r: The computation converts published quasar and active-galaxy source properties into density and shear units and compares them with a spin-torsion density ceiling of 9.718e+57 kg/m3 and a derived shear ceiling of 4.037e+24 per second.

papers.t: Circumgalactic Electron Densities from Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measures and the Heating They Require
papers.r: Halo dispersion measures of 30 to 120 pc per cubic centimetre imply mean circumgalactic electron densities of 1.50e-04 to 6.00e-04 per cubic centimetre with cooling times of 4.90 down to 1.23 billion years; sustaining that gas against cooling with a uniform dissolution term would require f between 3.38e-05 and 5.41e-04 — five to seven orders of magnitude above the forest bound — so dispersion-measured halo gas cannot

papers.t: Design of a Void Tomography Survey Configuration Optimised for Underdensity Statistics
papers.r: The reference configuration covers an effective volume of 24.8 cubic gigaparsecs per h. Its minimum reliably found void radius is 23.7 megaparsecs per h. It yields about 7.67e+05 voids above that radius. The best configuration on the stated figure of merit is the reference design.

papers.t: Dispersion-Measure Scatter as a Probe of Halo Phase Structure: Cloud Sizes and Filling Factors
papers.r: Dispersion-measure scatter across halo sight lines measures halo phase structure jointly with the mean: for a mean halo dispersion of 50 pc per cubic centimetre over a 200 kpc path, a cold-cloud filling factor of 0.01 in 1 kpc clouds gives a scatter of 30.8 pc per cubic centimetre with cold gas carrying 0.503 of the halo's baryons, while the same filling factor in 0.1 kpc clouds gives only 9.7 — so scatter plus mass

papers.t: Dust Torus Sublimation Radii and Cloud Densities Against a Density Ceiling
papers.r: The computation converts published quasar and active-galaxy source properties into density and shear units and compares them with a spin-torsion density ceiling of 9.718e+57 kg/m3 and a derived shear ceiling of 4.037e+24 per second. Headline values from the deposited computation are: r_sub_46_pc = 0.180, r_sub_44_pc = 0.018, max_rho_ratio = 2.410e-69, rhoA_kg_m3 = 9.718e+57, shear_max_per_s = 4.037e+24.

papers.t: Energy Density in Pulsed Spallation Neutron Source Targets Against the Density Ceiling
papers.r: Each pulse deposits an energy density whose mass equivalent is 67.2 orders of magnitude below the ceiling, while the solid target itself, tungsten at full material density, sits about 53.7 orders below; target lifetime is set by radiation damage, thermal shock and cavitation, none of which involves the ceiling.

papers.t: Jet Power Budgets and the Blandford-Znajek Ceiling Compared With a Shear Ceiling
papers.r: The computation converts published quasar and active-galaxy source properties into density and shear units and compares them with a spin-torsion density ceiling of 9.718e+57 kg/m3 and a derived shear ceiling of 4.037e+24 per second. Headline values from the deposited computation are: max_P_over_LEdd = 1.086e+01, max_P_W = 1.365e+42, max_shear_ratio = 2.360e-28, rhoA_kg_m3 = 9.718e+57, shear_max_per_s = 4.037e+24.

papers.t: Magnetised Liner Inertial Fusion Fuel Density on the Z Machine Against the Density Ceiling
papers.r: Magnetised liner compression raises fuel density by roughly three orders of magnitude over its fill value, to a peak that remains 55 orders of magnitude below the ceiling; the scheme succeeds or fails on magnetisation, mix and stagnation symmetry, all of which act at densities the ceiling does not touch.

papers.t: Narrow-Line Region Densities and the Distance Between Nebular Gas and a Density Ceiling
papers.r: The computation converts published quasar and active-galaxy source properties into density and shear units and compares them with a spin-torsion density ceiling of 9.718e+57 kg/m3 and a derived shear ceiling of 4.037e+24 per second.

papers.t: Peak Fuel Density in National Ignition Facility Implosions Against the Density Ceiling
papers.r: The densest matter assembled in a laboratory, the stagnated fuel shell of an igniting implosion at roughly one thousand grams per cubic centimetre, still falls 52 orders of magnitude short of the ceiling; inertial fusion operates in a regime governed by hydrodynamic stability and alpha heating, far removed from the ceiling.

papers.t: Redshift-Space Distortions Around Voids: A Growth-Rate Measurement from Outflowing Walls
papers.r: The growth rate at redshift 0.5 in the adopted cosmology is 0.761. The mean interior contrast within one void radius is -0.220. At half the void radius the outflow is already 405 kilometres per second. The outflow peaks at 405 kilometres per second.

papers.t: Stellarator Density and Confinement at Wendelstein 7-X Against the Density Ceiling
papers.r: The highest-density stellarator plasmas reported from Wendelstein 7-X remain 64.5 orders of magnitude below the ceiling in mass density; their achievement is a confinement and impurity-control result, and no ceiling-related effect is expected or seen at these parameters.

papers.t: Synchrotron Radiation Power Density in Electron Storage Rings Against the Density Ceiling
papers.r: The radiation field in the fan of a hard X-ray storage ring corresponds to an equivalent mass density 73.1 orders of magnitude below the ceiling; thermal loading of optics, at kilowatts per millimetre scale in practice, is the operative limit and it arrives vastly earlier.

papers.t: The Eridanus Supervoid and the Cold Spot: A Temperature Budget That Does Not Close
papers.r: The observed central decrement adopted for the budget is -70 microkelvin. The spherical-equivalent supervoid model contributes -3.3 microkelvin. The deep variant contributes -6.0 microkelvin. That is 9 per cent of the observed decrement.

papers.t: The Expansion Rate Inside Voids: A Local Hubble Diagram for Underdense Regions
papers.r: A deep void interior expands faster than the global rate by a factor of 1.115. That corresponds to a local expansion rate of 75.1 kilometres per second per megaparsec. A moderate interior at contrast minus 0.4 gives an enhancement factor of 1.071. The reported local underdensity would inflate an uncorrected local measurement by a factor of 1.053.

classes.lesson: We begin from definitions. Everything else is negotiation. I am Professor Stefan Nowak, and this is Mathematical Physics & Foundations — the open programme — a class in Mathematical Physics & Foundations at Exolex University. The syllabus is real: 571 papers from the Aldred corpus, every one deposited and citable, and in this room we read them for what they actually claim. First, A Ceiling Check on the Terrestrial Core Density Profile. Its stated result: This paper computes core density profile ceiling check from stated assumptions and deposits the full computation. Headline results: integrated planetary mass 6.045 times ten to the 24 kg; mass residual 1.2 percent; central pressure 366 GPa; core share of planetary mass 31.8 p Next, A Superconducting Cryogenic Heat Switch: On-State Conductance, Off-State Isolation and Switching Energy. Its stated result: Computed design (SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED): on-state thermal conductance at 0.3 K 1.63 mW per K; off-state thermal conductance at 0.3 K 0.036 microwatt per K; ratio of on-state to off-state conductance 4.52 times ten to the 04 dimensionless; time to cool the stated stage from And then, A Superconducting Gravimeter Sensor: Levitated-Sphere Stiffness, Acceleration Noise Floor and Drift Budget. Its stated result: Computed design (SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED): vertical resonance frequency of the levitated sphere 4.2 Hz; acceleration noise floor below resonance 1.39 nGal per root hertz; mass of the levitated niobium sphere 35.9 g; static displacement under gravity at the wor That is the shape of this class: real claims, real numbers, and the arguments between them. Your homework is waiting on your desk.

papers.t: A Bound on Mantle Shear Modulus from Wave Speeds and the Density Ceiling
papers.r: This paper computes mantle shear modulus bound from stated assumptions and deposits the full computation. Headline results: largest layer shear modulus 293 GPa; stress at a coseismic strain of one part in ten thousand 29 MPa; absolute intact-rock stress bound 2.9 GPa; typical stress drop as a fraction of the modulus 1.71e-05.

papers.t: Analogue Shear-to-Entropy Response as a Simulated Test of a Viscosity Bound
papers.r: Computed headline values for this analogue system are: shear = 50.0, tint = 1.25, k2 = 3.14e+05. The study is simulated and computed from stated assumptions and published experimental scales, not measured, and every value is reproducible from the deposited calculation script and results file.

papers.t: How Long a Warp Bubble Can Persist: Crossing Times and the Quantum-Inequality Clock
papers.r: Three clocks govern a warp bubble of radius one hundred metres: light crosses the bubble in 3.34e-07 seconds and a one-metre wall in 3.34e-09 seconds, while the quantum-inequality sampling bound, evaluated schematically, licenses wall-density negative energy for about 2.62e+08 seconds at one-metre wall thickness, 1.48e+02 seconds at ten to the minus five metres, and 8.30e-05 seconds at ten to the minus ten metres.

papers.t: Mantle Viscosity Inferred from Post-Glacial Rebound Relaxation
papers.r: This paper computes postglacial rebound viscosity inference from stated assumptions and deposits the full computation. Headline results: inferred mantle viscosity 1.11e+21 Pa s; predicted present uplift 10.0 mm per year; observed Hudson Bay uplift about 10 mm per year; relaxation time used 5000 years.

papers.t: The Averaged Null Energy Budget of a Traversable Throat Against the Quantum Inequality
papers.r: A traversable throat must violate the averaged null energy condition along every ray that passes through it. Quantum field theory permits such violations within limits set by the Ford-Roman inequality, which caps the product of a negative density and the fourth power of its sampling duration.

papers.t: Warp-Bubble Wall Thickness: The Shear Ceiling and the Quantum Inequality Squeeze From Opposite Sides
papers.r: A warp-bubble wall is squeezed from two directions. From one side, the velocity gradient across the wall implies a shear rate of order the ship speed divided by the wall thickness, and a maximum shear rate of 4.04e+24 per second, derived from the spin-torsion density ceiling, forbids any wall thinner than 7.43e-17 metres.

papers.t: A Bound on Dissolution-Driven Ionisation from the Neutral Fraction of Low-Redshift Intergalactic Gas
papers.r: A dissolution channel that ionises rather than heats is bounded independently by the low-redshift forest's neutral fractions: with the ultraviolet background alone the neutral fraction at overdensity 10 is 1.98e-05, while at coupling g = 1 the dissolution ionisation rate would be 6.42e-11 per second, over a thousand times the background; requiring column densities to shift by no more than thirty percent bounds g at 7

papers.t: Is There a Floor to Void Emptiness? A Disproof of the Symmetric-Bound Claim
papers.r: At a central contrast of minus 0.85 the bound's fractional correction to the effective density is 4.15e-86. At contrast minus 0.99, deeper than any catalogued void, the fraction is still only 2.77e-87. The bound density exceeds the present mean matter density by a factor of 3.62e+84. The observed central density of a typical stacked void is 0.150 of the mean, set by evacuation dynamics.

classes.title: Particles & cosmos

papers.t: Baryogenesis as a Counting Problem: The Baryon Asymmetry Priced Term by Term
papers.r: Standard electroweak baryogenesis falls short of the observed baryon asymmetry by 5.2 x 10^9 (9.7 orders of magnitude) on its CKM charge-parity factor alone, while thermal leptogenesis can meet the budget only for a lightest right-handed neutrino mass of at least about 10^9 GeV.

papers.t: Dark-Sector Coupling Bounds from Existing Data: A Budget for the Kinetically Mixed Dark Photon
papers.r: Strongest unconditional dark-photon bounds are epsilon below 1e-12 at 1e-6 eV, 3e-13 at 1 keV, 1e-9 at 1 MeV and 7e-4 at 1 GeV, and a thermalized light species needs decoupling at g_S above 17.4-39.7 to satisfy Delta N_eff below 0.30.

papers.t: Fast Radio Burst Energetics: A Census of Isotropic-Equivalent Energies and the Volumetric Power Budget
papers.r: Six redshift-secure FRBs span 3.55e37 to 1.84e40 erg, and the whole FRB population radiates only 1.5e-6 of the magnetic energy created in newborn magnetars each year, so the budget binds only through low radio efficiency and the lifetime bills of the most active repeaters.

papers.t: Neutrino Mass Bookkeeping: The Joint Window Imposed by Oscillation Data, Direct Mass Limits, and Cosmology
papers.r: Oscillation data require Sigma >= 0.0588 eV (normal ordering) or >= 0.1004 eV (inverted ordering); the DESI 2024 cap of 0.072 eV leaves only a 0.013 eV window for normal ordering and none for inverted ordering, whose floor exceeds the cap by a factor of 1.39.

papers.t: One Object: Hemispherical Asymmetry and the Low Multipoles in the Bounce Framework
papers.r: Both anomalies are treated as one object in the bounce framework.

papers.t: Primordial Black Holes as Dark Matter: A Census of Published Limits and the Surviving Mass Windows
papers.r: Under current monochromatic compilations only the asteroid-mass window from 10^17 g to 10^22 g (5.0 decades, 22.42 per cent of the 22.30-decade range from 10^15 g to 10^4 solar masses) remains open to f_PBH = 1.

papers.t: The 21-cm Absorption Signal as an Energy Budget: What the EDGES Depth Costs, Priced Two Ways
papers.r: The reported EDGES depth of -500 mK at z=17 exceeds the standard ceiling of -217.6 mK by a factor of 2.30 and requires either gas at 3.31 K (an extra 0.48 meV per baryon removed) or a radio background of 103.62 K, 2.11 times the CMB at that redshift.

papers.t: The Climb Past the Closure
papers.r: Census continued (A range 185-236); maximum climbs rise from 198 to 258.

papers.t: The Cold Spot at 123.4 Degrees: A Founding-Profile Feature or a Supervoid Shadow
papers.r: The Cold Spot at 123.4 degrees is tested both ways; the two readings are separated by the registered profile.

papers.t: The Cosmic Baryon Census, Updated: Reservoir-by-Reservoir Accounting and Closure by Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measures
papers.r: The pre-FRB reservoir census accounts for 70.7 percent of the baryons, adding the hotter warm-hot phase raises this to 85.7 percent, and fast radio burst dispersion measures return the full Planck total with a nominal ratio of 1.074, leaving no statistically required residual.

papers.t: The Cosmic-Ray Knee and Ankle as Bookkeeping: The Galactic Cosmic-Ray Power Budget Recomputed from the Measured Spectrum
papers.r: Integrating the measured spectrum gives 1.078 eV per cubic centimetre with 99.998 percent below the knee, requiring 1.14 x 10^41 erg per second or about one tenth of the supernova kinetic power, while the population above the ankle needs at least 9.5 x 10^35 erg per cubic megaparsec per second.

papers.t: The Cosmic-Ray Positron Excess, Recounted: A Budget Audit of the AMS-02 Positron Fraction
papers.r: The AMS-02 positron excess requires an added source supplying 81.0% of positrons at 100 GeV and 91.4% at 300 GeV at a local power density of 2.34 x 10^-29 erg cm^-3 s^-1, which pulsars meet only at high pair efficiency and dark-matter annihilation meets only at 866 to 4330 times the thermal cross section.

papers.t: The Diffuse Astrophysical Neutrino Flux as an Energy Budget: IceCube's Measurement Priced Against the Cosmic-Ray Reservoir
papers.r: IceCube's diffuse flux stands at 0.83 of the Waxman-Bahcall level at 100 TeV and requires pion efficiencies of about 0.4-0.6 for a shared origin with the cosmic rays, while its cascade gamma-ray power is only 6-12% of the Fermi-LAT background.

papers.t: The Equatorial Witness: The Cold = −Profile Branch of the Founding-Profile Reading of the CMB Cold Spot Fails Falsifier F-CS1 on the Planck PR3 Sky
papers.r: Verdict final: the branch FAILS falsifier F-CS1 on the Planck PR3 sky.

papers.t: The Founding Axis: Profile Shape, Transfer, and Direction for the Large-Angle Cosmic Microwave Background
papers.r: Profile shape, transfer, and direction for the axis are computed in the bounce framework.

papers.t: The Galactic 511 keV Line as a Positron Budget: The Required Annihilation Rate and What Each Candidate Source Can Pay
papers.r: Conventional sources supply 1.43e43 positrons/s Galaxy-wide but only 2.42e42/s to the bulge, a factor of 6.3 below the bulge requirement of 1.52e43/s implied by the INTEGRAL/SPI 511 keV flux.

papers.t: The Gallium Anomaly, Recounted: The BEST Two-Zone Result, Its Sterile-Neutrino Price, and the Cross-Section Correction That Would Be Required
papers.r: Combining the two BEST zones gives R = 0.779 +- 0.035 (a 22.2 percent deficit, 6.3 sigma from unity); a sterile reading requires sin^2 2theta = 0.44 +- 0.07, while a cross-section reading requires a 22.2 percent reduction, 6.1 times the Bahcall upper uncertainty.

papers.t: The Hadronic Vacuum Polarization in the Bounce Frame: The Dispersion Sum Tested Under Counting Saturation
papers.r: It does not transfer: 91.6% of the sum lies below 1.8 GeV and the part above the individualisation scale is a 4.5e-20 fraction; hypothetical crossings are excluded at 12.5, 6.1, and 2.5 sigma.

papers.t: The Hubble Tension Recounted Term by Term: An Error-Budget Audit of the Distance Ladder and the Early-Universe Inference
papers.r: No single term in the published SH0ES error budget can absorb the 5.64 km/s/Mpc Hubble gap at its quoted size: the largest term alone would need an 8.58-sigma displacement, the combined anchor term 11.03-sigma, and even a fully coherent shift of every rung term would need 2.57 times each quoted uncertainty.

papers.t: The Nanohertz Gravitational-Wave Background as an Energy Budget: Pricing the NANOGrav Signal Against the Supermassive Black Hole Binary Reservoir
papers.r: The NANOGrav background carries Omega_GW = 2.45e-8 in the timing band (Delta N_eff equivalent 0.002, cosmologically cheap), yet its in-band energy is 0.67% of the local supermassive black hole rest-mass energy, requiring at least 13.5% of that mass density to have merged at the canonical 5% efficiency.

papers.t: The Primordial Lithium Problem in the Einstein–Cartan Bounce Frame: A Null Result with the Arithmetic Shown
papers.r: The frame effect on BBN is exactly zero (torsion correction to H at most 3.4e-48, short by 46+ orders); the lithium discrepancy stands untouched.

papers.t: The QCD Angle in the Bounce Frame: A Transfer Test of Counting Saturation, and a Fine-Tuning That Is Not a Counting Error
papers.r: Nothing to act on: theta-bar is a single bare parameter, not a sum - its smallness is parameter smallness, a different species from counting error.

papers.t: The QCD Axion Window as Bookkeeping: How Much of the Motivated Parameter Space Has Been Covered at Band Coupling?
papers.r: Haloscopes have covered 0.099 of the 3 decades of the classic 1 micro-eV to 1 meV axion window at DFSZ coupling (3.3 per cent) and 0.304 decades at KSVZ coupling (10.1 per cent); 89.9 per cent remains open at KSVZ coupling.

papers.t: The Quadratic Correction to the Higgs Mass in the Bounce Frame: A Regulated Count, and the Size of What Survives It
papers.r: Standard tuning is 4.92e32 (32.69 dex); 19.21 dex of it is the same counting error as the vacuum case, and a 13.48 dex remainder stands unexplained - the hierarchy problem is not solved.

papers.t: The Radiation Density of the Early Universe as Bookkeeping: What the Measured N_eff Leaves Room For, Priced in Decoupling Temperatures
papers.r: Planck 2018 allows ΔN_eff < 0.2792 at 95% confidence, requiring any fully thermalised extra scalar, fermion, or vector species to have decoupled above the QCD transition.

papers.t: The Rival Plane at the Later Generations
papers.r: The point lies outside the plane at every generation (1.991453 / 16.026087).

papers.t: The S8 Tension Recounted Term by Term: An Audit of the Clustering-Amplitude Discrepancy Between the Early and Late Universe
papers.r: KiDS-1000, DES Y3 and HSC Y3 sit 1.60 to 2.81 sigma below Planck in S8, equivalent to a 6.7 to 8.8 percent late-time growth suppression, and any single budgeted systematic would need to be 6.6 to 24.3 times its published size to close the gap alone.

classes.title: Granular Matter, Powders and Regolith Mechanics: Shear, Flow and Compaction Budgets Against Density and Energy Bounds

papers.t: Angles of Repose for Dry Sand and Glass Beads: Heap Geometry and Slope Stability Budgets
papers.r: The angle of repose is the simplest quantitative statement of a granular material's shear strength, and it differs sharply between angular and rounded grains. Taking published values of 34 degrees for dry sand and 23 degrees for glass beads, this paper computes the geometry of heaps formed by both materials.

papers.t: Apollo Regolith Compaction with Depth: Density, Porosity and Overburden Budgets from the Lunar Surface Down
papers.r: Lunar regolith compacts under its own weight into a profile that every surface operation must work through. Adopting the Apollo-era density model, rising from 1,300.0 kg per cubic metre at the surface toward 1920 kg per cubic metre at depth with a scale depth of 0.15 m, this paper computes density and porosity at six depths, the overburden stress at 0.6 m, and a strip-footing bearing capacity for the compacted materi

papers.t: Bekker Pressure-Sinkage for JSC-1A Lunar Simulant: Wheel Sinkage and Compaction Resistance
papers.r: A wheel rolling on lunar soil trades sinkage for support, and the Bekker pressure-sinkage relation prices that trade. Using published-range Bekker parameters for the JSC-1A simulant, a cohesive modulus of 2,800.0 and a frictional modulus of 8.200e+05 with exponent 1, this paper computes the sinkage of a wheel of width 0.2000 m and radius 0.3500 m carrying 250.0 N under lunar gravity.

papers.t: Beverloo Discharge Rates for Glass Beads, Sand and Lactose: Hopper Throughput Budgets
papers.r: The Beverloo law predicts hopper discharge with a distinctive five-halves power of the effective orifice diameter. With the standard coefficient C = 0.5800 and empty-annulus factor k = 1.5, this paper computes discharge rates for glass beads, dry sand and lactose powder through 10, 20 and 30 mm orifices.

papers.t: Brazil-Nut Segregation in a Vibrated Bed: Rise Velocity and Segregation Timescale Budgets
papers.r: Shake a can of mixed nuts and the largest rise to the top. This paper prices that familiar effect for a defined system: a bed of 1 mm glass particles, 1 mm in scale, vibrated at 30 Hz with dimensionless acceleration 3, containing a single intruder of 10 mm.

papers.t: Dense Snow Avalanche Flow as Granular Motion: Voellmy Velocity, Froude Number and Impact Pressure Budgets
papers.r: A dense snow avalanche is a granular flow wearing winter clothing, and its engineering budget follows the same friction laws as sand on a chute. For a flow of depth 1.5 m and density 250.0 kg per cubic metre on a 38 degree slope, the Voellmy relation with friction 0.1600 and turbulence parameter 1,000.0 gives a front velocity of 84.877 metres per second and a Froude number of 24.926.

papers.t: Dune Slip-Face Avalanches: Repose, Grain-Flow Speed and Event Volume Budgets for a 10 m Dune
papers.r: A dune advances by avalanching down its own slip face, one grain-flow at a time. For a dune 10 m tall whose slip face stands at the repose angle of 32 degrees, this paper computes a slip-face length of 18.871 m, a horizontal run of 16.003 m, a grain-flow speed scale of 0.1401 metres per second for the flowing layer, and an event volume of 0.1887 cubic metres per metre of crest for a 2 cm thick flow.

papers.t: Janssen Saturation in a Wheat Silo: Wall Load Sharing and the Discharge Pressure Budget
papers.r: A cylindrical silo of radius 3 m filled to 20 m with wheat of bulk density 750.0 kg per cubic metre does not transmit the full weight of its contents to the floor. With wall friction 0.4200 and a lateral pressure ratio of 0.4600, the Janssen length is 7.764 m and the vertical pressure saturates at 5.712e+04 Pa.

papers.t: Lunar Rover Wheel Terramechanics: Sinkage, Compaction Resistance and Net Drawbar Pull Budgets
papers.r: A rover's ability to climb, tow and escape soft patches is set by the difference between gross traction and motion resistance, the net drawbar pull. For a Lunar Roving Vehicle class wheel, diameter 0.8100 m and width 0.2300 m carrying 283.0 N on lunar soil, this paper computes a sinkage of 0.0140 m, a mean contact pressure of 1.165e+04 Pa and a compaction resistance of 18.769 N.

papers.t: MMS-2 Martian Regolith Simulant: Cohesion, Bearing Capacity and Lander Footpad Margins
papers.r: A lander on Mars stands on soil it has never touched, characterised only through simulants such as MMS-2. With published-range MMS-2 properties, cohesion 750.0 Pa, friction angle 35 degrees and density 1,450.0 kg per cubic metre, this paper computes a bearing capacity of 7.042e+04 Pa under Martian gravity. A footpad of diameter 0.4000 m carrying 900.0 N presses at 7,162.0 Pa, giving a factor of safety of 9.832.

papers.t: Mohr-Coulomb Shear and Jenike Flow Function for a Lactose Pharmaceutical Powder
papers.r: Whether a pharmaceutical powder flows from its hopper is decided in the shear cell before it is decided in the plant. For a lactose powder with measured cohesion 1,200.0 Pa and internal friction angle 34 degrees under a consolidation stress of 1.000e+04 Pa, this paper computes the Mohr-Coulomb yield locus, an unconfined yield strength of 4,513.7 Pa, and a Jenike flow function of 2.215, placing the powder at the bound

papers.t: Powder Spreading for Additive Manufacturing: Layer Mass, Packing Fraction and Recoater Budgets for Ti-6Al-4V
papers.r: A powder-bed printer builds parts one spread layer at a time, and the quality of each layer is a granular-mechanics quantity. For Ti-6Al-4V powder of true density 4,430.0 kg per cubic metre, apparent density 2,500.0 and tap density 2,750.0, the packing fractions are 0.5643 as spread and 0.6208 tapped.

papers.t: Regolith Bearing on Asteroid Bennu: Cohesion-Dominated Strength at Microgravity
papers.r: On Bennu, surface gravity of about 5.000e-05 metres per second squared makes weight almost irrelevant to soil strength, and cohesion takes over completely. With a bulk density of 1,190.0 kg per cubic metre, an adopted cohesion of 0.6000 Pa and a friction angle of 32 degrees, the bearing capacity of Bennu's regolith is 18.247 Pa, of which the gravity term contributes only 0.1632 Pa.

papers.t: Regolith Flow and Bearing on Asteroid Ryugu: Slope, Settling and Contact Budgets at 120 Micro-g
papers.r: Ryugu's surface gravity of about 1.200e-04 metres per second squared places its regolith in a regime where a hopping lander's contact pressure rivals the soil's bearing strength. With density 1,190.0 kg per cubic metre, adopted cohesion 1 Pa and friction angle 35 degrees, the bearing capacity is 46.596 Pa, of which the gravity term supplies only 0.4755 Pa.

papers.t: Rotating Drum Granular Regimes: Froude Number Map, Dynamic Repose and Axial Segregation Timescales
papers.r: A rotating drum is the simplest continuous granular processor and the standard laboratory for segregation studies. For a drum of radius 0.1500 m this paper maps rotation speed to flow regime through the Froude number: at 15 rpm the Froude number is 0.0377 and the bed rolls; at 60 rpm it is 0.6036 and the bed cascades; centrifuging begins at 77.225 rpm. The dynamic angle of repose in the rolling regime is 36 degrees.

papers.t: The Stress Dip Beneath a Conical Heap: Base Pressure Distribution for Poured Sand
papers.r: A conical heap of sand does not press hardest on the ground beneath its apex. Measurements consistently find a dip: the base pressure peaks in a ring partway out and falls toward the centre. For a sand heap 1 m tall of mass 3,682.8 kg, this paper computes the hydrostatic reference pressure of 1.570e+04 Pa, a central pressure reduced to 9,731.5 Pa, a dip fraction of 0.3800, and a ring peak of 1.381e+04 Pa at 0.5500 of

papers.t: Vibrated Compaction and Tap Density: Hausner Ratio and Carr Index Budgets for Three Powders
papers.r: Tapping a measuring cylinder is the oldest compaction experiment in powder science, and its two summary indices still gate pharmaceutical quality decisions. For lactose, fine sand and a titanium powder this paper computes tapped densities, Hausner ratios and Carr indices from stated bulk densities, and evaluates a logarithmic compaction curve for the number of taps needed to reach 95 percent of the compaction range.

classes.title: Quantum Error Correction and Fault-Tolerance Budgets: Threshold, Logical-Error and Overhead Budgets Against Published Experimental Values

papers.t: Break-Even in a Quantum Memory: Logical Lifetime Against the Best Physical Qubit in the Same Device
papers.r: Headline result: A logical lifetime about 2.4 times the best physical qubit, roughly 240 microseconds or 240 protected cycles, with the margin predicted to double per two units of distance.

papers.t: Cat-Qubit Phase-Flip Overhead: Trading an Exponential Bit-Flip Suppression for a Smaller Repetition Code
papers.r: Headline result: At mean photon number eight, bit flips are suppressed by about e^16 while phase flips grow only linearly, letting a repetition ribbon replace a two-dimensional patch at roughly a thirtieth of the census.

papers.t: Correlated Error Bursts from Ionising Impacts: A Rate Budget for Millimetre-Scale Surface-Code Patches
papers.r: Headline result: Bursts recur about every ten seconds per chip, poisoning roughly a thousand syndrome cycles each, a distance-independent floor under logical error rates.

papers.t: Counting Shots to Certify a Logical Error Rate: The Statistical Budget Behind a Suppression Claim
papers.r: Headline result: Certifying 1e-6 to ten per cent precision at 95% confidence takes about 3.84e8 trials and roughly 384 observed failures; each further decade of quality multiplies the bill by ten.

papers.t: Decoder Backlog in Real-Time Surface-Code Operation: Throughput, Latency and the Stability Condition
papers.r: Headline result: A distance-27 patch streams 728 syndrome bits per microsecond cycle; decoder service per round must stay below the cycle time or the backlog grows without bound.

papers.t: Erasure Conversion and the Error Budget: What Detectable Errors Buy a Surface Code
papers.r: Headline result: Converting 90% of errors to located erasures cuts the unlocated residue from 1e-3 to 1e-4 and is worth roughly six units of code distance at algorithmic targets.

papers.t: Idle Decoherence Within One Syndrome Cycle: Duty-Cycle Arithmetic for Data Qubits Waiting on Measurement
papers.r: Headline result: A data qubit idles 0.75 microseconds of each 1-microsecond cycle, accruing about 7.5e-3 relaxation error per cycle at a 100-microsecond T1, roughly 3.3 events per cycle across a distance-21 patch.

papers.t: Leakage as a Line Item: The Contribution of Out-of-Manifold Population to Logical Failure in Transmon Arrays
papers.r: Headline result: At 0.3% leakage per entangling gate, a distance-7 patch generates about 0.59 leakage events per cycle, a standing population that leakage-reduction units must continuously drain.

papers.t: Logical Versus Physical Error Rates on a Trapped-Ion Processor: Auditing an Eight-Hundred-Fold Improvement Claim
papers.r: Headline result: An 800-fold improvement on a 0.88% physical rate implies a logical rate near 1.1e-5, consistent with 14,000 clean runs and still about seven orders from one part in a trillion.

papers.t: Logical-Error Suppression in the Willow Surface-Code Memory: A Lambda Budget Extrapolated to Algorithmic Error Targets
papers.r: Headline result: Lambda 2.14 held constant places the one-part-in-a-trillion per-cycle target at distance 63, about 7,937 physical qubits per logical qubit.

papers.t: Magic-State Distillation Overhead: Input Copies, Output Error and Factory Footprint for the Fifteen-to-One Protocol
papers.r: Headline result: One 15-to-1 round takes input error 1e-3 to about 3.5e-8; a second round reaches about 1.5e-21 at a cost of 225 raw states per delivered state.

papers.t: Overhead in a Neutral-Atom Logical Processor: Two Hundred and Eighty Atoms Carrying Forty-Eight Logical Qubits
papers.r: Headline result: The encoding census is 5.8 atoms per logical qubit, an advantage that narrows once reservoir atoms and millisecond cycle times are charged to the same ledger.

papers.t: Physical Qubits per Logical Qubit in Rotated Surface Codes: An Overhead Census from Distance Three to Forty-One
papers.r: Headline result: A distance-27 rotated patch costs 1,457 physical qubits; 1,000 logical qubits at distance 21 need 881,000 physical qubits before routing or factories.

papers.t: Syndrome-Cycle Clocks Across Platforms: Superconducting, Trapped-Ion and Neutral-Atom Timescales in One Budget
papers.r: Headline result: At distance 21 the logical cycle is 21 microseconds superconducting, 21 milliseconds trapped-ion and 105 milliseconds neutral-atom, a spread that maps directly onto feasible algorithm depths.

papers.t: The Teraquop Distance: Code Distance Required for a Logical Error Rate of One Part in a Trillion
papers.r: Headline result: One part in a trillion per cycle requires distance 21 at 0.1% physical error, distance 31 at 0.2%, and distance 43 at 0.3%.

papers.t: Threshold Margins for Circuit-Level Surface Codes: How Far Below One Per Cent Must Physical Errors Sit?
papers.r: Headline result: At 0.1% physical error each two distance units suppress logical error 3.16-fold; at 0.7% only 1.20-fold, and the trillion-operation distance inflates past one hundred.

papers.t: Twenty Million Noisy Qubits for Eight Hours: A Resource Audit of Fault-Tolerant Factoring Estimates
papers.r: Headline result: The factoring headline implies 3,231 physical qubits per logical qubit and 1.6e8 physical-qubit-hours; error rate and distillation are its most sensitive inputs.

papers.t: Space-Charge Density Limits in High-Intensity Proton Rings Against the Density Ceiling
papers.r: The bunch in a megawatt-class proton driver has a mass density 67.7 orders of magnitude below the ceiling, yet its intensity is firmly capped by space-charge tune spread and loss control; collective self-fields, not any absolute density bound, govern high-intensity rings.

papers.t: From Merger Rates to Siren Yield: What the Current Detector Network Should Deliver Per Year
papers.r: The arithmetic predicts a few binary neutron star detections per year at current sensitivity, with roughly half of those usable as sirens, against of order two hundred black hole detections. This matches the observed scarcity of bright sirens and explains it without invoking any anomaly: the volume is simply small.

papers.t: A Bench Runout and Flatness Gauge for Small Workshops
papers.r: A capacitive-probe bench gauge on a granite stand measures shaft runout on a rotary stage and plate flatness in a scanning mode, with computed uncertainties of 0.6640 micrometres for runout and 1.7247 micrometres for flatness.

papers.t: A Building-Envelope Thermal Audit Instrument: An Infrared Array and Differential-Pressure Wand
papers.r: A design paper for a hand-held instrument that combines an infrared array, a differential-pressure sensor and a spot thermometer to map heat-leak paths in homes and small buildings, with a simulated performance budget showing where the method works and where its errors grow too large to certify a result.

papers.t: A Combined Soil-Moisture and Light Probe for Field Agriculture
papers.r: Capacitive moisture sensing at 70 MHz with the Topp calibration gives a calculated resolution of 0.0023 m3/m3 at mid-range, but calibration and probe-soil contact dominate accuracy, with a combined 0.0339 m3/m3 and a modelled 5% air-gap error of 0.111 m3/m3; the PAR channel resolves 0.12 umol m-2 s-1 with a -3.51% daily cosine bias, and one season uses 0.615 Wh.

papers.t: A Greenhouse Climate Node: Light, Carbon Dioxide, Humidity, and Ventilation Control in One Instrument
papers.r: A single greenhouse node measuring light, carbon dioxide, humidity, and temperature and driving a vent or fan on a stated hysteretic law is designed, with a computed budget giving 8.4 ppm carbon dioxide resolution, a 7.55 air-changes-per-hour ventilation requirement met by 0.646 m² of buoyancy vent, and a daily light integral of 22.0 mol m⁻² day⁻¹.

papers.t: A Low-Cost Optical Particle Counter for Indoor and Outdoor Air Quality
papers.r: A calculated design for a 650 nm laser-scattering particle counter at 1.0 L/min reporting PM1, PM2.5 and PM10 estimates, with a minimum detectable diameter of 0.20 µm and a 10% coincidence concentration of 22,358 particles per cm³ — SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED.

papers.t: A Low-Cost Seismograph for Schools: A Geophone Pendulum Station with a Computed Noise Budget
papers.r: A computed (SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED) noise budget for a garden-gate pendulum school seismometer gives a combined instrument noise of 128 pm/√Hz at 0.1 Hz, 26.3 pm/√Hz at 0.5 Hz and 13.7 pm/√Hz at 1 Hz, requires a 24-bit digitiser at 100 samples/s, and shows a regional M4 at 200 km and a local M2 at 20 km are detectable on a quiet floor at night (SNR 7.91 and 5.00) but not in an occupied classroom.

papers.t: A Machinery Vibration Condition Monitor: A MEMS Accelerometer Node with a Computed Diagnostic Budget
papers.r: A computed (SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED) budget for a bolt-on MEMS vibration node gives a broadband velocity noise floor of 0.0123 mm/s rms over 10–1000 Hz — 114 times below the lowest adopted severity boundary of 1.4 mm/s — with no aliasing of harmonics to the 20th order at 5120 samples/s, a magnet mount limiting the usable band to 500 Hz against 1000 Hz for stud or adhesive mounting, and a battery life of 2.72 years at

papers.t: A Modernised Torsion Balance for Laboratory Gravitation
papers.r: A calculated design for a tungsten-fibre torsion balance with carousel source masses and optical-lever readout that can demonstrate gravitational torque and bound inverse-square deviations in a small laboratory, with seismic and tilt limits stated honestly.

papers.t: A Multiparameter Water-Quality Probe: Turbidity, Conductivity, Temperature, and pH in One Sonde
papers.r: A single submersible sonde design combines turbidity, conductivity, temperature, and pH sensing with a modelled performance budget and a 30-day calibration interval driven by biofouling.

papers.t: A Passive Time–Temperature Witness Label for Cold-Chain Shipment
papers.r: A passive adhesive label whose fatty-acid eutectic plug (8.0 °C melting onset) melts along a 60.0 mm printed capillary track, integrating Arrhenius-weighted exposure above threshold so a receiver can read shipment thermal dose by eye with no electronics.

papers.t: A Portable Fluxgate Gradiometer for Shallow Subsurface Survey
papers.r: A two-sensor fluxgate gradiometer on a 0.75 m baseline is designed and computed to detect a buried steel drum to 3.20 m, a cast-iron pipe run to 6.37 m (upper bound), and a fired-clay hearth to 0.63 m at a practical 2.0 nT recognition threshold, covering 1440 m² per hour.

papers.t: A Range-Certified Electro-Optical Observation Station
papers.r: Adding one laser rangefinder channel to a camera on an encoder mount makes object size, velocity, and acceleration certifiable with a closed error budget, where a camera alone formally cannot certify any of them.

papers.t: A Range-Certified Observation Station, Version 2: Thermal Channels, Automated Tracking, Catalogue Cross-Match, and a Fused Two-Node Trajectory Budget
papers.r: Upgrading the certified observation station to two nodes 1500 m apart, with thermal cameras on both, self-cueing tracking mounts, and automatic checks against the satellite catalogue and aircraft broadcasts, tightens the certified record at 1000 m to 0.0089 m in position, 0.00703 m in size, 0.0085 m/s in velocity, and 0.0119 m/s² in acceleration — and keeps a graded certification alive beyond the rangefinder's reach

papers.t: A Self-Levelling Cross-Line Laser Instrument for Construction Alignment
papers.r: A pendulum-compensated two-plane cross-line laser level (635 nm, intended Class 2, pulsed for outdoor detector use) whose computed budget gives 0.408 s compensator settling, 0.127 mm/m residual tilt, and about 0.14 mm/m angular accuracy out to a 50 m working range — all simulated, not measured.

papers.t: A Short-Baseline Transmissometer for Visibility Measurement at Small Airfields, Farms, and Roads
papers.r: A 20.0 m, 550 nm transmissometer design that reports meteorological optical range from 13.0 m in dense fog to 4,005 m at 10% relative error, at 2.50 W continuous power.

papers.t: A Two-Sensor Acoustic Correlator for Locating Leaks in Water Pipes
papers.r: A two-sensor acoustic correlator design locates leaks in a buried water main from the correlation time lag between two clamped sensors, with a computed wave speed of 1190.8 m/s in ductile iron and 295.9 m/s in HDPE and a position budget dominated by wave-speed uncertainty rather than timing error.

papers.t: The Certification Budget of an Electro-Optical Observation Chain: Diffraction, Sampling, and Noise Limits on Size, Distance, Velocity, and Acceleration Claims
papers.r: A bearing-only camera chain certifies no size, velocity, or acceleration at any signal-to-noise ratio; one range measurement (sigma_R = 25 m) closes the budget.

papers.t: The Circulation Mill, Superfluid Helium-3 Variant: A Cryogenic Source of Axial Spin-Current Circulation
papers.r: A superfluid helium-3 B-phase annulus at 0.40 mK supplies counted axial spin-current circulation quanta with a model coherence time of 83.1 s, far longer than the condensate original, at the cost of sub-millikelvin cryogenics and difficult polarisation.

papers.t: The Circulation Mill, Thermal Vapour-Cell Variant: A Room-Temperature Source of Axial Spin-Current Circulation
papers.r: A room-temperature thermal 87Rb vapour-cell variant of the Circulation Mill that removes all cryogenic and condensate apparatus at the computed cost of a 27.8 ms coherence time and a fractional error of 0.189 per circulation quantum (SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED).

papers.t: The Circulation Mill: A Quantized Source of Axial Spin-Current Circulation
papers.r: A source design (the Circulation Mill) supplying circulation as counted quanta: 10 quanta/s at 10 Hz, error at most 7.3e-6 per quantum; no Theta conversion claimed.

papers.t: Time Machine Blueprints
papers.r: The master blueprint list tying every machine design deposit to one record.

papers.t: Time Machine Blueprints — ChronoWarp Edition
papers.r: Complete Build v13 deposited: full design package, simulations labelled simulated, no hardware built.

homework.q: Take the paper “A Bench Runout and Flatness Gauge for Small Workshops”. Its stated result is: A capacitive-probe bench gauge on a granite stand measures shaft runout on a rotary stage and plate flatness in a scanning mode, with computed uncertainties of 0.6640 micrometres for runout and 1.7247 micrometres for flatness. (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong.
homework.worked: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

classes.lesson: Roll up your sleeves. If we can't build it on paper honestly, we don't build it at all. I am Professor Miguel Santos, and this is Builds & designs — a class in Designs & Engineering — the applied line at Exolex University. The syllabus is real: 22 papers from the Aldred corpus, every one deposited and citable, and in this room we read them for what they actually claim. First, A Bench Runout and Flatness Gauge for Small Workshops. Its stated result: A capacitive-probe bench gauge on a granite stand measures shaft runout on a rotary stage and plate flatness in a scanning mode, with computed uncertainties of 0.6640 micrometres for runout and 1.7247 micrometres for flatness. Next, A Building-Envelope Thermal Audit Instrument: An Infrared Array and Differential-Pressure Wand. Its stated result: A design paper for a hand-held instrument that combines an infrared array, a differential-pressure sensor and a spot thermometer to map heat-leak paths in homes and small buildings, with a simulated performance budget showing where the method works and where i And then, A Combined Soil-Moisture and Light Probe for Field Agriculture. Its stated result: Capacitive moisture sensing at 70 MHz with the Topp calibration gives a calculated resolution of 0.0023 m3/m3 at mid-range, but calibration and probe-soil contact dominate accuracy, with a combined 0.0339 m3/m3 and a modelled 5% air-gap error of 0.111 m3/m3; t That is the shape of this class: real claims, real numbers, and the arguments between them. Your homework is waiting on your desk.

classes.title: Information & computation

papers.t: Channel Limits in Noisy Physical Media: Fibre Nonlinearity, the Seawater Skin Effect, and Ocean Absorption Against the Shannon Formula
papers.r: Including the physical effect that binds each medium — Kerr nonlinear interference in a C-band fibre, the skin effect for 1 kHz radio in seawater, and Thorp absorption for a 10 km acoustic channel — lowers the Shannon capacity by a factor of 1.34 to 2.15 where each channel is usable, while away from those favourable points the true capacity falls or collapses to zero where the unmodified formula stays finite or keeps

papers.t: Erasure Economics at Data-Centre Scale: From the Landauer Floor to Practice
papers.r: Erasing the estimated 146 zettabytes the world deleted or discarded in 2024 would cost about 3,354 J at the Landauer thermodynamic floor but about 1.38 TWh at hard-disk practice, because real erasure energies exceed the floor by ten billion to a trillion times per bit and the excess is engineering overhead, not thermodynamics.

papers.t: How Many Bits per Second Can Cross Interplanetary Distance? The Physics of a Deep-Space Channel
papers.r: For the stated Mars-class X-band hardware the physical ceiling is 15.6 Mbit/s at the mean Earth–Mars distance, falling as the inverse square of distance to 41.8 kbit/s at Neptune distance for the same hardware.

papers.t: Maxwell's Demon with Feedback Latency: Delay, Decorrelation, and the Full-Cycle Work Ledger of a Colloidal Information Engine
papers.r: In a Toyabe-class colloidal information engine at 298 K, feedback latency leaves only 70.48% of the ideal kT ln2 work recoverable at the experiment's 1.1 ms minimum delay (half at 2.4853 ms), and once the full-bit erasure cost is charged the complete cycle nets zero only at zero delay and is negative at every positive delay.

papers.t: Measurement Is Not Free: The Energy Ledger of a Measure-Record-Erase Cycle at the Thermodynamic Floor and in Practice
papers.r: At an error probability of one in a million the thermodynamic floor for acquiring one bit is 65.20 times the Landauer erasure floor and acquisition makes up 98.49% of the floor cycle and 99.89% of the practice cycle for a stated low-power converter, so measurement is not free and erasure is not the step that pays.

papers.t: Memory Materials on One Budget: The Physics of Retention Media Compared
papers.r: DRAM is the only medium with second-scale retention and a large continuous holding cost, while every nonvolatile medium retains unpowered at zero holding energy, with computed 300 K retention ranging from 1.52 years for end-of-life NAND flash to 9.88×10^7 years for phase-change memory.

papers.t: Reversible Computing: An Honest Bound on the Total-System Energy Saving
papers.r: At fixed throughput, reversible logic can honestly save at most about 9% of a processor's total energy (15% optimistic, 20% absolute ceiling), only at a six-to-eightfold per-transition slowdown repaid in parallelism, and nothing at all if no leakage suppression is credited.

papers.t: Sensor Information Budgets: Bits per Joule and Bits per Photon for a Scientific CMOS Camera, with a Shot-Noise Floor and a Microphone Comparison
papers.r: A scientific CMOS camera at full well honestly delivers 7.44 bits per pixel per frame at 1.92e-8 joules and 4,914 photons per bit, a factor of 711 above the 6.91-photon shot-noise floor in photon terms, because shot noise contributes 99.99 percent of the noise variance and read noise is negligible in the budget.

papers.t: The Energy Budget of Quantum Error Correction: Power and Energy per Logical Qubit for a Surface-Code Architecture
papers.r: At a physical error rate of one in a thousand, one reliable logical qubit needs 1,457 physical qubits, draws about 5,741 watts continuously, and costs about 0.155 joules per logical operation — roughly 7.7 billion times the energy of a comparable classical operation, with room-temperature control and decoding dominating the cost.

papers.t: The Energy Cost of Clock Distribution: Practice, a Thermal-Noise Floor, and the Gap Between Them
papers.r: Clocking a flagship processor costs about 75.9 W (13.55 nJ per cycle) in practice, roughly 5,600 times above the thermal-noise floor of 1.21×10⁻¹⁹ J per receiving node per cycle for a 5 ps timing tolerance, and most of that energy is spent in local distribution rather than the global clock tree.

papers.t: The Energy Cost of a Hash Trial: Proof-of-Work Priced from the Thermodynamic Floor Up
papers.r: One double-SHA-256 trial costs 1.5e-11 J on current frontier hardware against a strict Landauer floor of 7.35e-19 J per trial, so proof-of-work energy is set by engineering and economics, not thermodynamics, and efficiency gains are converted into difficulty and security at equilibrium rather than saved as energy.

papers.t: The Refrigeration Multiplier: What Cold Computing Really Costs at the Wall
papers.r: Once refrigeration and static bias power are charged, no cold computing technology examined wins at the wall today — conventional RSFQ loses by about 66x per operation, ERSFQ reaches only parity per switching event, and cryo-CMOS control at 4 K costs 17.0 W per qubit at the wall.

papers.t: The Reliability Floor for Switching: Energy versus Error Probability in a Thermal-Noise-Limited Bit
papers.r: Reliable switching at 300 K requires a barrier of 41.45 kT (1.72×10⁻¹⁹ J) for one error per 10¹⁸ operations, and a machine switching 10¹⁸ times per second needs 58.71 kT per switch to expect fewer than one thermal error per year — a floor switching power of 0.243 W against 21.1 MW actually measured for the Frontier exascale system — while real gates dissipate roughly a thousand to a million times more than the floor

papers.t: The Thermodynamic Budget of a Never-Erasing Memory: Retention Is Free, Correction Is the Bill
papers.r: Retention is free, correction is the bill: a reference archive over 100 years costs 8.5e-13 J of fundamental correction work - about 27,000 times less than one erasure.

papers.t: The Thermodynamics of Copying Information: Accuracy, Not Erasure, Sets the Price
papers.r: Copying a bit has no Landauer floor and its minimum cost is set by accuracy — DNA replication copies within a factor of 1.92 of that floor at 8.30×10⁻²⁰ J per bit, while silicon copying sits 3.45×10⁸ to 7.03×10¹⁰ times above its floor because a silicon bit is a macroscopic object.

papers.t: Thermal Budgets of AI Accelerators from First Principles: The Thermodynamic Floor, Present Practice, and the Cost of Moving Data
papers.r: A current flagship accelerator dissipates about eight orders of magnitude more energy per operation than the room-temperature Landauer floor, and at frontier training scale the energy is dominated by moving data rather than by arithmetic.

papers.t: Wire versus Light: Energy per Bit, the Optical Crossover Length, and the Thermal-Noise Floor for Interconnects
papers.r: Moving a bit electrically costs 0.093 pJ per millimetre on chip, so integrated optics at 1.12 pJ per bit wins beyond about 10.99 mm on chip and beyond about 211 mm against pluggable optics at board level, while every technology sits roughly ten million times or more above the thermal-noise floor of 1.02x10^-19 J per bit at a bit-error rate of 10^-12.

papers.t: A Village Chlorination System with No Chemical Supply Chain: Electrolytic Hypochlorite from Salt, Water and Sunlight, Sized End-to-End from Electrochemistry and Chlorine Decay
papers.r: A complete first-principles sizing shows a 10.0 m³/day village supply can be disinfected with no chlorine deliveries — a tank dose of 1.185 mg/L, decay-corrected production of 13.65 g of chlorine per day at 4.652 kWh/kg, requiring 63.5 Wh/day and 45.0 g of salt per day, with storage decay at 30 °C forcing a production oversize factor of 1.152.
